name: Christ in the Old Testament
about: Types, shadows and prophecies fulfilled in Christ.

teachings.title: Anointed with the oil of gladness
teachings.summary: The anointing of the king in Psalm 45 pictures Jesus anointed by the Spirit without measure, exalted after the cross, who gives believers the anointing of the Spirit by faith.
teachings.text:
After establishing His love for righteousness, the text states that He is anointed with the *oil of gladness* and that His garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia.

As messianic prophecy, the elements of His anointment listed are symbols of Jesus, His death and His triumph over death.

The oil of gladness, olive oil, used to anoint kings and in celebration. To freshen the face, and to signify joy.

We see throughout scripture that oil is used as a metaphor for the Spirit. And Jesus, at the start of His ministry is anointed by the Spirit from the Father, showing to John and the other witnesses that Jesus was the Christ.

**Matthew 3:16-17**
*And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

While earthly kings were anointed with physical oil, Jesus was anointed directly by the Holy Spirit without measure.

**John 3:33–35**
*He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him. The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.*

And so, the ultimate joy, the true anointing Is given to Jesus the Christ.

**Philippians 2:8–10**
*And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth*

The meekness of the sinless Son of God, going to the cross, despising the shame to be raised into glory, as the King of righteousness. The truth by which we are set free.

**Isaiah 61** says that He that was anointed by the Spirit of God to *preach good tidings to the meek..bind up the brokenhearted...proclaim liberty to the captives,* and to give unto them that trust in that truth..*.the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.*

The Messiah, the Anointed One, the Christ gives us the anointing of the Spirit by faith, that we may be His fruit, the trees of righteousness, planted that He might be glorified.

teachings.title: My God, why hast thou forsaken me
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically gives Christ's cry from the cross, when bearing the sin of all mankind as our scapegoat and High Priest He was forsaken by the Father that we might live.
teachings.text:
*Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?*

In the 9th hour, Jesus cried out from the cross the words of the Psalm, the opening line of a song of desperation, penned by David centuries earlier.

An event recorded twice in the gospels:

**Matthew 27:46**
*And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

**Mark 15:34**
*And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

The man Christ Jesus, after a day of betrayal, abuse, beaten beyond human recognition, scourged, shamed and mocked, cursed, hung on the tree, and become sin for all mankind, acknowledging in death that, by taking on all of the sin in all of creation, He is, in that moment, no longer looked upon by the Father Whom He has been with, and a part of, since everlasting.

The prophetic words of the Psalm, Christ's words echoed through time to the psalmist, words Jesus Himself knew from before the foundation of the world, conveying the heartbreaking moments before the perfect and holy Lord would willingly give His life that we may live.

Jesus cried out in Aramaic, the daily language of the people, the language He grew up in life speaking, conveying His humanity in that moment.

The Hebrew words, long sung by Israel in the congregation, translated, and again, interpreted into Greek, and given to us in English, never losing a scintilla of power. Given to us as the blessed hope, an example of the endurance and steadfastness we should look to:

**Hebrews 12:2-3**
*Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds*.

Jesus, our scapegoat, receiving our sin in atonement, without the camp. Taking them utterly away. Not as the blood of bulls and goats, offered yearly for sanctification by the High Priest of the Tabernacle, but once and for all, shed for man. And He, as THE High Priest, entered into the Heavenly Tabernacle, and applied His own precious blood upon the mercy seat in Heaven.

No greater love than this has ever been shed towards us, that God became flesh, and lived among us, sinless and perfect, that He might drink of this cup. Going to the cross that we might live.

The tragic nature of these words reveals the depth of the love of God. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

teachings.title: Psalm 22 and the sufferings of the cross
teachings.summary: Psalm 22 prophetically pictures the mockery, piercing, thirst and parted garments of Christ's crucifixion and the anguish He bore all His life, before turning to the hope that all things work together for good to them that love God.
teachings.text:
The prophetic nature of the God-inspired Psalm of David continues, showing the children of Israel the truth of Christ, through a glass darkly. In David's personal pain, we see a shadow of the suffering of Jesus, a reproach of men, despised of the people, laughed to scorn.

**Matthew 27:39–43**
*And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads, And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross. Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.*

Compassed about by bulls, by dogs, men like lions, surrounded by the Roman soldiers doing the work of the Jews, piercing Jesus' hands and feet with nails. Splayed out upon the cross, His joints distended and twisted to support the weight of His body. The sinking feeling of death settling in His guts, as He struggled to breathe. His bones in sharp relief to His stretched out skin.

Crying out for water, Jesus is given vinegar to drink, raised up on hyssop, a bitter gall that could not quench His overwhelming thirst. The soldiers then parted His garments by lot:

**Matthew 27:34–35**
*They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink. And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.*

The desperation and loneliness, the mental anguish Jesus suffered on the cross, He had also carried with Him for 33 years. Understanding the suffering that awaited Him at Calvary, knowing His anointed part in the great redemptive plan, while at all points being touched by the infirmity of the flesh, and tempted as we are. His prayers at Gethsemane, Son to the Father, that if it were possible to take this cup from Him, please let it be so. But steadfast to do the will of the Father, even knowing the physical and emotional pain He would endure. These stanzas in this psalm tragically capture it all, before transitioning to the joyful hope found in every tribulation those who love God can take comfort in:

**Romans 8:28**
*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

teachings.title: Save, LORD: the name of Christ in Psalm 20
teachings.summary: Psalm 20 is praise for salvation in the name of Christ Jesus, the one offering, whose soul was not left in hell.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 20** is yet another song of praise and worship for the salvation that is in Christ Jesus.

The name of the God of Jacob. The Lord that strengthens us out of Zion. The one offering forever, the burnt sacrifice. Christ Jesus.

The love of God has been granted to us in his grace, and his counsel is wisdom; trust in the Lord.

We will rejoice in the salvation given to us in the name of our God. We will set up banners in His holy name. He is Christ Jesus, and God hears all our petitions, lifted up in His name.

The Lord saves His anointed. He did not leave his soul to see corruption. His anointed was not left in hell. The saving strength of His right hand. Christ Jesus.

Some trust in the power of this world, their own strength, their own works. And they will be brought down low. He will say depart from me. I never knew you.

But to those of us who trust in the name of the Lord, our God, we are risen and made to stand upright. In Christ Jesus.

Save, Lord. In the name of the King of Kings and the Lord of lords, Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: Jesus dumb before His accusers, appointed to destruction
teachings.summary: Christ, silent before Pilate and Herod, fulfilled Isaiah 53 and Lemuel's charge to open the mouth for the dumb, leaving the rulers of Judea without excuse.
teachings.text:
**Vs 8-9** *Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.*

The call to be a voice for the condemned without a voice, for the poor and needy, is the way of Kings and pleasing to God.

Jesus, appearing before the judgment spoke not at all.

**Matthew 27:12-14**
*And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee? And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.*

Jesus, appointed for destruction and mute to give His cause, directly exemplifies this saying. While Pilate could be excused for not knowing the proverbs (or the prophecy;
**Isaiah 53:7** *He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.*) Herod, King of the Jews, and the presits and scribes should have.

**Luke 23:8-9**
*And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him. Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.*

A fit ruler should speak for the condemned, to ensure justice. To consider the judgment. To plead the cause of those brought before them by the powerful, to ensure the poor and powerless aren't being falsely accused.

The knowledge given to Lemuel by his mother was certainly heard by those princes of Judea, by their King, and ignored. What should have convicted them in the heart, witnessing Jesus, silent before them, instead was an indictment, that they had no excuse.

teachings.title: Wisdom from everlasting is the Word
teachings.summary: Wisdom in Proverbs 8, crying out to all and with God from everlasting before creation, is the Word, Jesus Christ, the way, the truth and the life.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 8 (& 9)**, are an Ode to Wisdom, the Word and Spirit of God, with Him in the beginning , through Whom all creation was made.

Wisdom cries out from all creation, from the top of the mountains, in the high places and in the paths. The Lord's way is wisdom. In the coming and going of the city. At its gates and doors.

Like God calls to all men, as Jesus lifted up, wisdom calls out to all. To the simple and fools. To those who love wisdom and seek her excellent things, her right things. To those that seek truth.

**John 14:6** *Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.*

**Matthew 7:7** *Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you*

**John 8:32** *And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free*

The words of wisdom are the word of God, and there is nothing perverse or froward in them. Holy and plain to those that listen.

More precious than any treasures, wisdom is better than gold. With wisdom dwells prudence; Wisdom applied to practice. Discernment and action according to knowledge.

The wise hate evil; pride and arrogance, froward mouths they hate.

By wisdom kings and princes rule.

*I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me*.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.

**Psalm 63:1** *O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is*

The Lord's wisdom is from everlasting, His word. Before all creation, He is. Eternally with Him, as one brought up together.

**John 1:1-2** *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.*

Blessed is the man who finds wisdom. They receive life and favor of the Lord. They live in His grace.

But woe to those that hate wisdom. *All they that hate me love death.*

teachings.title: The cornerstone laid before the foundation
teachings.summary: God's answer from the whirlwind points to Christ the chief cornerstone laid at creation, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world, with the sons of God being believers rather than angels.
teachings.text:
*Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind.*..

The storm that gathered as Elihu spoke, which the boy used as it came to lecture Job with what he thought was profound wisdom, brings with it the voice of God. And He sets to immediately show the shallowness of Elihu and the three friends' thinking.

*Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?*

What a terrifying moment, to know that God will demand answers of you. And this fear should grip all men, that they believe on Christ, to avoid that fierce judgment, where all will be asked of those not found in His book of Life, by the omnipotent God of all.

He laid the foundations of the earth, the breadth and scope of creation was measured out by Him. The foundations of the world are set by Him, and the cornerstone thereof.

*Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.*..

**1 Peter 2:6-8**
*Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.*

The morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy and the truth of Jesus Christ, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The cornerstone laid, upon Which all is built.

(I believe this is a OT prophecy of Christ, Who has been since before creation, but Who IS and was born of men, to die and rise again. That the stars are the hosts of Heaven. That the sons of God are those from Adam who believed. Some think this is literally creation, and so the sons of God must be angels, to whom at no time did God call sons, according to scripture.)

From the seas to the shores to the heights of the sky, to the position of the stars in the sky, God has set all things, and the paths thereof.

The wonder of creation is not only in the placement of these things God created, but in their paths and purposes. Time itself is a testimony of His power.

The day chasing away the darkness. The rivers carrying the floodwaters to the sea. The voice of thunder, and the rain upon the wilderness, making it spring to life. The pictures of God's mercy and wrath, revealed. Made manifest that no man has an excuse.

Only God can create these things, and not as man would, even if we could. For the Lord knows the beginning from the end. The order He has made is greater than our ability to comprehend.

Creation isn't like the birth of man. Flood waters are pictured in birth, but is not the birth. There is no womb that could create the frost. The hail which will be used in due time by the Lord in His wrath. Rain isn't called and lightning ordered and arrayed, but by the living God.

God has even put what we call the food chain in its place, that the beasts of the world eat, even as they don't sow or reap. But that He opens death to all, that they may eat.

And this same God puts wisdom in man's heart.

teachings.title: How can man born of woman be clean
teachings.summary: Bildad's question how man born of woman can be justified is answered in Christ, made a little lower than the angels, born of woman yet pure, who tasted death for every man (Hebrews 2).
teachings.text:
Bildad's short response to Job is less accusatory, and more reflective after Job's previous statements on the nature of God, His wrath on the unrighteous, and the hope of salvation.

He comments on the power and holiness of the Lord, His hosts of Heaven, His great light more pure than the sun and moon.

His question, with a God so pure and holy, how can man be justified with God? How can any man be clean that is born of women. That men are worms before Him.

But even in this rhetorical question, God shows us His plan. To be made little lower than the angels. To be born of woman and be pure. To be a son of man, a worm, bearing the reproach of men, and yet Jesus was made hope from the womb.

Pierced hands and feet. Garments parted by lot. And still, raised from the dead, declaring the deliverance of the meek, those that fear Him, to all kindreds, the Governor among nations. The Lord. A generation of people who were not a people, declaring His righteousness.

**Hebrews 2:1-13**
*For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.*
 *For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings. For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.*

teachings.title: My witness is in heaven
teachings.summary: Job's lament prefigures Christ's sufferings, and his witness on high is Christ the advocate pleading for sinners.
teachings.text:
*Then Job answered and said, I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.*

And isn't that the whole of the matter, the failure of Job's friends to comfort him in his affliction, rather than accuse him in their hypocrisy.

He says that if the roles were reversed, he could speak as they do, shaking his head in judgement, but he wouldn't. Job would try to assuage them. He has been made weary and beaten down by such desolate company.

His face and body bear record of Job's suffering and the wrath against him.

*He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me. They have gaped upon me with their mouth; they have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully; they have gathered themselves together against me. God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.*

This is, of course, literally the feeling of Job in his wretched condition, yet he speaks in the Spirit throughout, and it is difficult not to see Jesus' suffering in this entire exchange. *He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground.*

But as prophetically accurate, it still is Job's lament, *My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?*

He has mourned as a man mourns, and in sackcloth and dust. His face foul of weeping, and his eyelids darkened as it were the shadow of death. His prayers are ernest and sincere. He just wants to know why, and be comforted.

And in all that, the faith of Job is clear, *Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high.* This is Jesus and His wonderful advocacy for us sinners before the judgment of God. Job is certain of that, despite all else.

He laments, crying out that his friends scorn him even as he calls out to God.

*O that one might plead for a man with God, as a man pleadeth for his neighbour!*

An indictment of the three, but also an appeal to Christ the mighty councilor.

teachings.title: Seeing Christ in Job is no anachronism
teachings.summary: The Old Testament is all about Christ, so Job's Holy One and Redeemer is Christ and OT saints were saved by the same faith in the same Savior.
teachings.text:
Many argue that Jesus wasn't known in the Old Testament, that salvation by faith didn't exist. That it is an anachronism to see Jesus in Job, and *the Holy One*.

There is no anachronism when we see Christ in in the Old Testament. It is entirely about Him.

He is the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The same Word who was with God and was God, Who walked in the furnace with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

He was the Rock in the wilderness.

Job’s cry a few chapters from now, “I know that my Redeemer liveth” being about Christ is not an anachronism or a theological reach; it is an inspired revelation.

When Job clings to the Holy One as his strength and hope beyond death, he is laying hold of the same eternal Christ who is the substance of every shadow, the end of every type, the answer to every promise.

The Old Testament saints were saved by the same faith, looking to the same Savior, the same redemption, if through a veil that has now been torn.

teachings.title: The messenger and the Lord coming to His temple
teachings.summary: Malachi 3 foretells John the Baptist and Christ coming to His temple, who will come again as refiner and judge.
teachings.text:
The burden of the Lord upon Malachi continues, and the prophecy of Christ Jesus.

That a messenger would come before Him, John the Baptist, and the Lord shall suddenly come into His temple. Fulfilled both literally and in coming in the flesh. His body a temple.

The messenger of the covenant. The promise kept, and a new covenant made.

He shall come. And as that promise was kept, so shall He come again. Sitting as judge. As a refiner of silver and of gold. As fuller's soap makes garments white.

The offering made in righteousness. His body and blood. An offering pleasant to the Lord.

He says, judging Judah that they have withheld in tithe and offerings. Robbing God, and will be sifted as wheat for it. Verse 5 reminds me of **Revelation 21:8**

*But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.*

The immutable God, He changes not.

 He again calls for repentance towards Him, to turn again to the Lord of hosts, but they would not.

The unbelieving, calling faith vain. Scoffers as in the last days. They call the proud happy! "Gay pride." They promote those who work wickedness.

But those who fear the Lord are His, and His promises to us are true. That all who seek Him are found and made sons of God. Spared as sons, from our sins. Amen

teachings.title: Smite the shepherd: the wounds in His hands
teachings.summary: Zechariah 13 foretells Christ pierced and wounded in the house of His friends, the smitten shepherd whose fountain cleanses His people.
teachings.text:
**Zechariah 13** continues the prophetic vision of the previous chapter, and builds upon it. In that day, they look upon the one they pierced, the one they sold for 20 pieces of silver, the one who fulfills the promise to David of an eternal King, the promise of a high priest forever, that breaks the staff of "Beauty," that is the old covenant, that breaks the staff of "Bonds" that separates Jews from Israel, that puts families apart from one another, bringing division even among father and son, mother and daughter, the good shepherd, will bring forth a fountain of living water. He *will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications,* and their sin and uncleanliness will He remember no more.

The false gods will be cut off, their idols gone, no remnant of their religion or the prophets that spoke lies will remain.

*And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.*

Jesus, wounded for our transgression, by His stripes are we healed.

Smite the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered.

**Matthew 26:31**
*Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.*

The unbelieving will be cut off, the third part refined as with silver, or with gold. And *they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.*

Amen

teachings.title: Thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter
teachings.summary: Zechariah 11 prophesies judgment on Judah's false shepherds and the breaking of the covenant, and his price of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter is fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of the Good Shepherd.
teachings.text:
Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah.

The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun.

The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them.

These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock.

And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of **Jeremiah 3:15**

*And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding*.

So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event.

God will feed the flock to the slaughter.

This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel.

**Luke 21:21-22**
*Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands."

He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off.

He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord.

Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious.

**Matthew 26:14-15**
*Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver*.

The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter.

**Matthew 27:3-7**
*Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.*

The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment.

teachings.title: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding upon an ass
teachings.summary: Zechariah 9 foretells Christ's entry into Jerusalem and His kingdom, and the war against Greece becomes the gospel's conquest, not modern Greater Israel.
teachings.text:
The burden of the word of the Lord, the inspired prophet speaking the word of God, saying that peace will be on the land, even to the cities of Syria, as all eyes of the nations will be as the tribes of Israel, being towards the Lord.

This establishes the prophetic sayings context, towards a future time when all men look to Christ. The greater border, to Tyre, cast down by the Lord despite its wealth, and to Gaza and Ekron, their kings deposed and the land made desolate. Ashod and the Philistines, all under the wrath.

This aspect of end times prophecy is cherry picked by modern Jews to justify their goal of Greater Israel. They seek to establish by their own works the Kingdom they've been cut off from. Of course it will come to naught.

When Christ establishes His millennial kingdom, the heathen against Him will be gone, leaving only remnants that are for the Lord.

*Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass*.

We all know the story from the Gospels, of Jesus triumphant entry into Jerusalem on the foal of an ass, cheered by the Jews who within a weeks time would cry, "Crucify Him!"

Jesus, who would deliver peace among the heathen, cutting off the oppression of the chariots and horses, the foreign armies against Israel, had they obeyed the conditional covenants and promises made by God.

Still, at His coming we will see Him establish His Kingdom, over the ends of the Earth.

By His blood, those prisoners of sin, oh wretched men that we are, set free from Hell. He says to turn to the stronghold, as prisoners of hope rather than sin, and He will render double unto thee. Great is His reward.

The Lord makes an allusion that Judah will be bent as a bow, with all Israel as the arrows. That Israel will be against Greece as a sword of a nighty man.

It is supernaturally inspired for Zechariah to mention Greece here. At the time of the prophet Zechariah, who is generally dated to around 520–518 BC, during the early Persian empire, Greece was not yet a dominant world power but was emerging as a significant cultural and political force. But it was fragmented city-states and not unified under Alexander yet.

As we have seen in Daniel, the Lord has predicted for them the rise of Greece as an empire, and its eventual role during the Ptolemaic period that followed Alexander the Great of destroying Zidon, Tyre, and taming of Syria and Egypt, Philistine and other enemies of Judah.

But, in the NT context of the Messiah, the war-like weapons of Jerusalem and Israel against the Greeks becomes a conquest by the gospel. The sword, the word of God.

The understanding that it is the Lord of hosts, Jesus Christ, Who is God, shall be their defense. Shall subdue all kingdoms, the King of kings, Lord of all. Not simply a human king. And all the people will rejoice at the harvest. Amen.

teachings.title: The Lord rebuke thee: Joshua made clean
teachings.summary: Joshua the high priest made clean without the temple pictures cleansing by grace through faith and points to Christ the Branch and corner stone, while railing against Satan is not God's way.
teachings.text:
**Zechariah 3** presents the prophet with a vision of the high priest Joshua, in the time of Zerubbabel and the restoration of the Temple in Jerusalem. And the angel of the Lord stood before him, and Satan at his right hand to resist him. To accuse him and tempt him.

The Lord rebukes Satan, the adversary, just as in **Jude,** where angels, even archangels, who all are mightier than man, don't bring railing accusations or curses against the Devil, but say "the Lord rebukes thee."

There are many who have built an entire ministry on the basis of "rebuking Satan," railing against the devil. Not resisting him, that he flees, but they themselves speaking evil of dignities, railing against things they don't understand. They often come with a false gospel, adding works or strange doctrines. Charismatics and charlatans.

But the Lord rebukes Satan here, saying that Joshua was an iron plucked from the fire. His instrument. Even as the Lord set His name on Jerusalem, so He had chosen Joshua to be His high priest.

In the vision, Joshua is arrayed in filthy garments. And those that stood before him are ordered to take them away, that the Lord would clothe him in a change of raiment. Making him clean.

Just as Jude writes of saving some by fear, pulling them from the fire, hating even the garments spotted by the flesh. Just as Jesus promises to clothe those who believe on His name in white.

For the priests of the Old Testament must be cleansed and sanctified, made holy by diverse washings and sacrifices, but Joshua, without the temple and without the purification rituals was made clean by grace through faith by the living God.

Joshua is given a fair mitre, a head covering for the office, and fine garments, as the angel of the Lord stood by.

And again, we are given a conditional promise to the high priest, *Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by.* The angels around him.

Then he is told through the prophet, that the Lord will bring forth His servant, the Branch, a promise of Christ Jesus. He says He will lay before Joshua a stone, that rock of salvation as Christ is called;

**Isaiah 28:16**
*Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.*

As in **1 Peter 2:6-9**
*Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light*

The image of Christ as the foundation, the corner stone, perfect and square, and the sanctification in Him of the royal priesthood, carrying over from the Old Testament, done away with, and given to a new priesthood of believers, washed clean in the blood.

The Lord of hosts says, *I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree.*

That blessed day, at the coming of the Lord of hosts. Amen.

teachings.title: The seventy weeks point to Jesus
teachings.summary: Daniel's 69 weeks from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem land on Christ's ministry and His being cut off, showing the power of God's word.
teachings.text:
I have to also point to the prophecy of Jesus' first coming. It is wild how God gave Daniel this vision of the "seventy weeks," laying out a timeline that points right to Jesus. Gabriel tells Daniel about 490 years—seventy weeks of years—starting from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem (around 457 BC, give or take, with Artaxerxes’ decree). Fast forward 69 of those weeks (483 years), and you land in the time of Jesus’ ministry, around 27-30 AD.

The Messiah is "cut off" being the crucifixion. God dropped a prophecy hundreds of years earlier, nailing the timing of His Son’s arrival and sacrifice.

Like in Isaiah and Jeremiah, God was saying, “I’ve got this all planned out, and I’m showing you I’m in control.”

The precision blows my mind—centuries before Jesus walked the earth, God gave Daniel the timing, and it played out just as He said.

Some folks debate the exact dates or lean into a future fulfillment, but seeing those 69 weeks line up with Christ’s coming? That’s the power of God’s Word shining through. It’s a reminder that when God speaks, it’s as good as done.

teachings.title: The stone cut out without hands
teachings.summary: The empires of Nebuchadnezzar's image came to pass, and Christ is the stone that breaks them and the head of the corner, so we cannot doubt God's promises.
teachings.text:
Now **Daniel 2** is a familiar story. King Nebuchadnezzar has a dream that troubles him, and he cannot recall what it was, but seeks someone to tell him the dream and its meaning.

And all the wizards and wise men of Chaldea cannot do this impossible task. The king orders that all his advisors be put to death for their inability to do this, including Daniel and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Rack, Shack and Benny).

But Daniel stays the hand of the man, Arioch the king's captain, by asking him to give Daniel time, and a promise that the Jewish eunuch could find out the kings dream and interpretation.

And in prayer the matter is made known to him by God. And he brings it to Nebuchadnezzar.

That the king dreamed of an idol, a collosal image. Head of gold, chest and two arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron and feet, iron mixed with clay.

And the interpretation thereof,

The Head of Gold: Babylonian Empire

The Chest and Arms of Silver: Medo-Persian Empire

The Belly and Thighs of Brass (Bronze): Greek Empire (Macedonian, under Alexander the Great)

Legs of Iron, the Roman Empire

Feet of Iron and Clay: the Roman Empire divided, and then scattered among the nations.

This is the history that came to pass.

And then we see Jesus. The stone cut from the mountain, without hands. The stone the builders rejected. The foundation upon which is built the everlasting Kingdom. Destroying the kingdoms of men.

**Matthew 21:42**
*Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

*Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.*

**Mark 12:10**
*And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner*

Peter to the Sanhedrin in **Acts 4:11**
*This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.*

Because we know the empires came to pass, and the truth of the prophecy, how can we doubt the promise of God in Christ?

Isn't it marvelous in your sight?

teachings.title: They always looked for the Christ
teachings.summary: It is false that Old Testament believers did not know a Christ would come; Moses, the prophets, Simeon and Anna looked for Him by faith.
teachings.text:
Jesus Christ, to Whom all the prophets gave witness. The redeemer of God.

**Luke 2:25-32**
*And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law, Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.*

The mistaken idea that no one in the Old Testament period understood that there would come a Christ, Who would be salvation to all who believed on Him, is false.

Moses and the prophets all gave witness to His coming. And though they saw it afar off, most dying in faith having not seen Him, but persuaded of Him, many, right up to the birth of Jesus and His coming into His glory, waited, watching for him.

**Luke 2:36-38**
*And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.*

They heard the word of God preached, and believed. Faith cometh by hearing the word of God. And there were people looking forward to their redemption. A light to the Gentiles. That all nations be blessed in Him. The mighty one of Jacob, the son of David.

They watched and waited for Him, just as we watch and wait for His return; By faith. Amen.

teachings.title: Prepare ye the way of the Lord
teachings.summary: Isaiah 40 foretells John the Baptist and Christ the Shepherd, shows the folly of images of God, and promises strength to those who wait on the Lord.
teachings.text:
We are there in **Isaiah 40**, and the Spirit of the Lord has poured forth out of the prophet, to speak to the fathers and those of us unto whom the end of the world has come. And what words of power and promise!

And praise God that *The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.*

The very nature of God revealed in this chapter, one of the greatest in the book of Isaiah, is echoed throughout scripture, especially the New Testament.

Beginning with an irony, telling the false prophets of Jerusalem to speak words of comfort, that she is pardoned. That their warfare is over. As Jeremiah will, years later, talk about the false prophets preaching "peace, peace."

But Judah, and eventually the world, will receive *from the Lord's hand double for all her sins.*

*The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God*.

A prophecy of John the Baptist, going before Jesus to make the King's Highway, the way of the Lord. Making the land flat, the way smooth, the lanes straight. In our hearts, that Jesus may come unto us. *And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed.*

*He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.*

Jesus is that good Shepherd. He directs the Spirit of the Lord, teaching all things.

**John 16:13-14**
*Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.*

And in the presence of the Lord God Almighty, by Whom all things are made, He counts all the nations, even Judah as so little as dust. A drop in the bucket.

*All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity*.

In His greatness, how can man seek to capture Him in an idol? Or an image? *What likeness will ye compare Him to?*

The Catholics and her harlot daughters, making images of God, Christ Jesus or of man, attempting to in their spiritual poverty, without an oblation, having not the sacrifice of Jesus, they seek a cunning work of men to take His place.

*Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?*

It is the Lord, from everlasting, Who has created all things, the gold and silver and trees and stone...they are nothing to the Living God.

All the wisdom and judgment of the earth is vanity.

God fainteth not. He never shall grow weary. But all our lives will wither and come to naught.

But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength. Our hope is in Him that never tires and Who created all things, and we shall be strong in Him. Never tire. Never be weary. Kept by the power of God. Amen

teachings.title: Jesus is the plumbline
teachings.summary: The plumbline set in Israel in Amos 7 is Jesus, the perfect cornerstone and measure of justice, while Bethel's false priesthood pictures Rome.
teachings.text:
Amos, preaching against Israel, at Bethel, the site of the false religion of Jeroboam. Where the idols and false priesthood that claimed to represent the true God of Israel were. Essentially, the Vatican for the Northern Kingdom. And Amos is preaching their doom.

He dreamt of grasshoppers destroying the latter growth of the second harvest. After the taxation of the King had taken his in the first harvest. Eating up what remained.

And the prophet prayed for his people, Judah, *O Lord God, forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small.*

Pleading for a savior. And God replies with another vision, of fire consuming a part of the deep. And again the prophet gave intercession for his people; *O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small.*

And the Lord repented. Changing His mind against the judgment that would have consumed all Israel. And He shows Amos another vision, the Lord standing upon a wall, set by a plumbline, a measure of perfect straightness and square. And the wall was built by this plumbline, set in the midst of the people of Israel, with the promise *I will not again pass by them any more*.

Jesus is that plumbline. The stone the builders rejected, perfect and square, the cornerstone upon which all is built. The guide to know perfect justice. The hope to rise up from Jacob.

For this the Lord repented, but not the entire judgment. The high places of Issac, that is Israel, shall be made desolate and the sanctuaries laid waste. And the house of their king, Jeroboam, slain by sword. All things we know followed in time.

The. Amaziah the false priest there in Bethel, maybe his generations "Pope," spoke out against Amos. Accusing him against the King for his preaching, and saying to go preach in Judah, for money. Accusing him basically of sedition against the Northern Kingdom, and that he only preached for filthy lucre. *O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there*.

Amos replies that he was no prophet, but was employed and had a living before being called of God to preach. For Amaziah's railing, Amos preaches harder against them, and says the priest's wife shall become a harlot in the streets of a polluted land, as Israel will surely be made desolate, carried away into captivity.

teachings.title: Micah 5: the ruler out of Bethlehem
teachings.summary: Micah 5 plainly foretells Christ's birth in Bethlehem, His smiting and His everlasting goings forth, so unbelieving Jews who deny He is in the Old Testament are liars.
teachings.text:
Here in **Micah 5** the prophet gives the word of God clearly and easily understandable to us, the coming of Christ Jesus in peace and deliverance, and His second coming, bringing wrath and destruction on the heathen nations.

There's prophecy about the end of Assyria, which was brought low by the Babylonians after its destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, keeping the Assyrians from doing the same to Judah. But primarily, this chapter is about Christ. It hardly needs any commentary, it is so clear.

Birth in Bethlehem. Smiting the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. The ruler coming forth from Judah who's going forth have been from old, from everlasting. Jesus.

The unbelieving Jews, so-called, who today say "Jesus doesn't appear in the Old Testament! None of the prophecies fit!" are liars. Antichrists. If they believed Moses and the prophets they'd believe on Him. But they reject the Son and have not the Father, despite being blessed with the oracles of God.

teachings.title: Out of Egypt have I called my son
teachings.summary: As God called Israel out of Egypt, so He called His Son, and as Israel turned from Him so Christ's own received Him not, though God chastens to bring men to repentance rather than to destroy.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 2:13**
*And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.*

Truly, as God called Israel out of Egypt, so too would the Father call His Son, Christ Jesus from the West, into the promised land.

And just as He came into His own, and the received Him not, Israelites turned away from the Lord to Baalim, and Baal Peor, and images and serving idols with incense.

The word of the Lord was given them, teaching Israel how to be healed, but they knew it not. He led them like cattle and led them with love and led them with freedom and liberty in Christ and with blessings of plenty, and still they didn't harken to Him. Instead, the backslid, and so Assyria would rule them, and the sword destroy them and their cities, all because of their own counsels, all by their own choice.

The Lord says it isn't His desire to destroy them for destruction's sake, to make them as Admah and Zeboim, as they were destroyed along with Sodom. He doesn't enter into the city as men, seeking to destroy, but as the Holy One, chastening them that they turn to Him again. To come to repentance towards the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ.

*Ephraim compasseth me about with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit: but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the saints.*

Israel may have chosen their own destruction, by lies and deceit and their lack of knowledge. But in Judah they yet ruleth with God, faithful with the saints, again pointing to the coming Messiah.

teachings.title: Rehoboam's heavy yoke and Christ's light yoke
teachings.summary: Solomon's reign pictures the millennial kingdom and his heavy yoke the law, while Christ offers the lighter yoke of grace and brings wrath upon the unbelieving world.
teachings.text:
Continuing the theme of **2 Chronicles** showing David as the first coming of Christ Jesus, Solomon's reign a picture of the millennial Kingdom, now we have Rehoboam, Solomon's son taking the throne, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat who was in Egypt for fear of King Solomon, loosed for a season and come, deceiving the people into rebellion against the King, to make himself King over Israel.

Of course the picture isn't precise, but we can see the outline and shape through the glass darkly.

The yoke of Solomon wasn't grievous. The people had wealth and servants and peace, but as a picture of the law, the yoke was indeed heavy. None being able to be saved by works of the Law.

Just as Jeroboam comes in his father's name, so too has Christ, and offered a lighter yoke; salvation by grace. Just as the wise advisors told the young King;  *be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them.*

But the young who advise him say make the yoke worse, and chasten not with whips, but worse, with scorpions.

The Father does chasten us, scourging every son. Jesus does being the wrath of God upon the unbelieving world, including scorpion-locusts from Hell.

Again it isn't a perfect one to one picture of things, but you can see the shape and draw the lesson.

teachings.title: Mount Moriah, where God provided a sacrifice
teachings.summary: The temple was built on Moriah where Abraham offered Isaac, a picture of Christ, and its cherubim were never bowed to, refuting idolaters who cite them.
teachings.text:
The construction begins, noting specific measurements and qualities of the decorative features and layout.

Some idolators justify their bowing and serving images of men by pointing to the decorative and illustrative placement of Cherubim and pomegranates in the Temple design. No Israelites bowed to these things, representative of the pattern in Heaven. They didn't offer prayers or sacrifice to them. They served no purpose other than to make the house of the Lord reflect His temple in Heaven.

The location of the Temple mount, Moriah, where the Lord appeared to David, and where the sacrifices to the Lord took place by the threshing floor of Orman, was also where Abraham brought Isaac to be sacrificed; **Genesis 22:1-2**

*And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.*

There, in a picture of Christ, where Issac, Abraham's only begotten son, carried the wood up the mountain to be offered, with hyssop and crimson. And God the Father provided a substitutionary offering, a ram in a thicket of thorns.

The same Jerusalem where Jesus was brought before the high priest, near Golgotha where He gave His life.

Likely the same place Melchizedek the King of Salem offered Abraham's sacrifice. Where Christ will return to rule and reign. The place God chose to place His holy name.

teachings.title: Jachin and Boaz, pillars of the promise
teachings.summary: The temple pillars Jachin (He will establish) and Boaz (in Him is strength) picture the promise and strength of the Christ to come.
teachings.text:
"According to the first-century Romano-Jewish scholar Josephus' book Antiquities of the Jews, **Jachin** (Hebrew יָכִין yakin "He/it will establish") stood on the right on the portico of Solomon's Temple, while **Boaz** (Hebrew בֹּעַז boʿaz "In him/it [is] strength") stood on the left, and the two were made by a Canaanite craftsman named Hiram."

The pillars stood outside the entrance, free standing. One to the North the other the South, in the East-facing entrance. East to catch the rising sun.

Where He will establish, where He is strength. A reminder of the testimony of Christ. The faith of redemption that all man has been saved by since Adam. The twin pillars are a picture of the promise and strength of the Christ to come.

It is unknown if these pillars made it into the design of the 2nd Temple, but their inclusion here in Chronicles, written for the admonition and instruction of those returning from Babylon makes it likely in my opinion.

We know from Jeremiah that they were destroyed and broken down at the beginning of the captivity, and the desolation of Jerusalem.

teachings.title: The son of David shall rule forever
teachings.summary: God's covenant with David that his son would build a house and reign forever is a clear picture of Christ, which is why the gospels' son of David is messianic.
teachings.text:
**1 Chronicles 17** finds David at his peak as King of Israel. He has power, a capital, great palaces and all from the anointing of the Lord. He sits with Nathan the prophet, and inquires about building a temple for God that He may no longer be in tents.

And just as in the same story found in **2 Samuel 7**, God speaking through Nathan tells David that he shall not build the temple, but makes instead a covenant with David that his son will, and that the son of David will rule forever. This is a clear picture of Christ.

The intended audience for the chapter were men of Israel returning from the captivity of Judah by Babylon, and God's mention of redeeming their fathers from Egypt was particularly fitting for them, as was the reassurance that the kingdom was blessed by God through David's son. That a Temple of God would be built. A house, just as the exiled were returned to rebuild.

But the same covenant is clearly speaking of Jesus, the house He shall build, the redemption He would pay for. That Jesus would be as a son to the Father. And rule and reign forever.

It is a beautiful passage, and you gain understanding of why when in the gospels people call Jesus the "son of David" there is a messianic meaning behind it.

teachings.title: The Prophet like unto Moses
teachings.summary: Moses foretold Christ the Prophet, and gave the test for false prophets that Jesus repeated: ye shall know them by their fruits.
teachings.text:
Moses, speaking of Christ, tells the people that the LORD will raise a Prophet from among them, speaking the words of God. There is also a dual fufiled prophecy here, regarding other prophets of the Lord that shall come, that they may be tested by what they preach, seeing if it is true. And a warning against the false prophets, and that those who are acting presumptuously, telling lies in God's name shall die.

It is the same warning given of Christ against false teachers; that you shall know them by their fruits. *If the thing follow not, nor come to pass*; if their preaching doesn't produce after the things of God, *ye shall know them.*

teachings.title: Stones at Pharaoh's gate a picture of Christ's coming
teachings.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's throne set on stones at Pharaoh's gate pictures Christ the King setting His throne on the lively stones of believers and destroying idols.
teachings.text:
Now the Lord says to Jeremiah, go to the gate of the Pharaoh in Egypt, and place great stones in the clay at the entrance, and preach that His servant, Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne upon these stones, and destroy Egypt, spoiling their cities, destroying their temples and burning their palaces. That the Chaldeans will slay whom God will, and lead captive whom He will. That the king will wear Egypt as a shepherd puts on a cloak.

In this, we see a picture of the coming of the Lord, Jesus Christ. Who is the King, the Father's servant. Who will build his throne on the lively stones of believers, upon the foundation laid by Jesus. In triumph over sin and death. Smashing idols, breaking the images of the false gods. Sending those who obeyed not the word of God to their destruction.

Amen

teachings.title: The covenants of David and Jacob fulfilled in Christ
teachings.summary: In promising to restore Jerusalem, God foretells Christ, in whom the covenants with David and the Levites are as sure as day and night.
teachings.text:
The Lord God is not slack concerning His promises. Here in **Jeremiah 33**, the word of God which had been against the people of Judah, as they were brought into captivity, has the people saying He had abandoned His covenant, that it wasn't their own violation that led them to this desolation and spoiling, but His. God continues to reassure through the prophet of their coming deliverance at the end of the 70 years, if they harken unto Him. If they keep His word and have faith in His promises. Even in this despair and tribulation.

And in His promise to restore life to the desolation of Jerusalem, God gives us yet another prophecy of Christ.

That the seed of David shall multiply, and the priests of Levites that minister to Him. David shall not want a man to sit up on the throne. The preists shall not continual sacrifice. God in His mercy shall forgive all sin and inequities. Just as the covenant of day and night shall not be broken, neither shall the covenants of Jacob and David, fufiled in Christ.

teachings.title: Jehovahjireh: the Lord will provide
teachings.summary: Abraham's offering of Isaac on Moriah, with the ram provided in his place, pictures God providing His only begotten Son as the sacrifice for sin.
teachings.text:
*Jehovahjireh*, the Lord provides. And *as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.*

The sacrifice of the only begotten to be a burnt offering. The wood, carried up the mount, which is Golgotha, in the land of Moriah, which is Jerusalem. The thicket of thorns on the young ram without blemish, offered in place of the son by God.

God created a covenant with Abraham based on the blood of Jesus Christ. The sacrifice that God provides, to take away the sins of the world. The symmetry and perfection of His promises, laid out over thousands of years, and continues to this day.

Jesus is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that sinful man may be reconciled with God.

Jehovahjireh.

teachings.title: This day is this scripture fulfilled
teachings.summary: Reading Isaiah 61 at Nazareth Jesus openly declared Himself the Christ, and when His own rejected Him He pointed to the Gentile widow and Naaman, prefiguring God's turn to the Gentiles.
teachings.text:
Now having established somewhat of a following throughout Galilee, Jesus returns to Nazareth, the town He grew up in. Where He lived as a child with Mary and Joseph, His half brothers and sisters. Where He developed the habit of going to synagogue. He returns full of the Spirit, and is called to read, and He preaches the prophecy of Christ from **Isaiah 61:1-2**
*The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;*

Note He leaves off the day of vengeance. That is His second coming. Here He is at His first.

**John 3:17**
*For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.*

And so, Jesus reads this scripture foretelling His coming, and says, with every eye on Him; *This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears*.

For those who doubt that Jesus ever proclaimed Himself to be the Christ, here He is saying precisely that. From the beginning. In no uncertain terms.

And the crowd becomes incredulous. "Is this not the Son of Joseph?" They knew Him, watched Him grow, saw Him in synagogue.

In response we are given the first record of Jesus preaching in Luke;

*Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country. And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.*

In **Mark 6**, we get more detail of this part; *A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.*

Basically, those who know us best, whose familiarity has them over comfortable in their understanding. Many Christians can relate to this, where after being born again we try to share the good news with relatives or friends, and they, knowing us intimately, scoff. "You? I saw you that one time..." Or even just see us as the child they watched grow and can't accept that you've got something to offer them in your youth. It's why it can be difficult for a Christian to get members of his own family saved.

And so, being rejected of His hometown crowd, Jesus doubles down and preaches even harder, using scripture. He says, citing **1 Kings 17**, you remember Elijah, how he was rejected and shut up the heavens that it didn't rain for 3 and a half years? That in Israel was great famine? The Spirit led the prophet to a Gentile widow in the land of Zidon who, along with her son was about to die of hunger, having only one meager meal left between them. God sent Elijah there because of her faith. In the story she offers the food to the prophet in faith, even though it was all she had. And God works a miracle where they are all fed and sustained with what little she had until the time of famine was over.

Jesus says, I bet there were many widows starving in Israel. But it was a Gentile woman who He saved.

Then, Jesus mentions **2 Kings** 5, and the prophet Elisha, where a Syrian, the captain of the hosts of the army of the king, suffered leprosy. Jesus says that many lepers were in Israel in the time, but it was this Gentile that God sent His prophet to heal.

That the prophets were rejected of their own, and so the healing power of God, His blessings and promises went to others. To Gentiles.

**John 1:11**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not.*

Jesus spitting fire, using scripture, He rebukes and reproaches His countrymen for their rejection of the word of God, the Gospel of truth He's brought to them, in a prefigure of the rejection He would face of the Jews at large, and prophesying God's turn to the Gentiles that would receive Him. And in a like manner, the crowd engaged at their own sin being pointed out, gathered to kill Jesus. They bring Him to the top of a hill, looking to cast Him off headlong.

teachings.title: Son of David and Son of God
teachings.summary: Luke's genealogy places Jesus in David's line as the promised King while He is also the Son of God, the two sonships of one who is fully God and fully man.
teachings.text:
Luke, having established the time and circumstances surrounding these events, then gives his version of the generations of Jesus, going from his stepfather Joseph's lineage. Perfect in his generations, all the way back to Adam, who we are reminded, was begat of God.

Being the son of Joseph, even adopted, places Jesus in line for the throne of David, fulfilling the prophets sayings that there will be a King from the root of Jesse, a descendant of David, who would rule and reign forever. The Son of David.

To the more secular, this places Jesus in line to be an earthly king. To make the Christ the physical deliverer of Israel. But to those called by the Spirit, and given understanding of scripture, the savior of their souls and heir to the Heavenly Kingdom. The Son of God.

It is these two sonships that Jesus was born into. Fully God. Fully man. And the conflict in the hearts of those who hear of Him, even those who directly saw Him walk among them performing miracles and preaching on the Kingdom of God, would set the stage for His ministry.

teachings.title: Zacharias Prophesies the Promise Fulfilled
teachings.summary: Zacharias shows in the Spirit that all the prophets' promises to Abraham, Moses and David are fulfilled as John prepares the way of Christ.
teachings.text:
We learn that Mary spent the remainder of Elizabeth's term with her, and departed. John is born and so named, as the angel instructed Zacharias.

When people who know them hear this, they question why. And when mute Zacharias writes in faith that his son's name is John, he is freed from the curse and able to speak again. And the Holy Ghost comes upon him, and he gives praise to God almighty, prophesying in His name;

*Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear, In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways; To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins, Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.*

This is the promise of the Lord given witness by all the prophets. Don't miss this. Zacharias is showing, in the Spirit, how all is being fulfilled. With the mercy of God is with them. That his son shall prepare His way. To give knowledge of salvation, by the remission of sins. A light. A guide. Showing the way of peace. Because in sin, man is at enmity with God. But in Christ, God is offering peace on earth, goodwill towards man.

This is what was promised Abraham. Moses. David. All the prophets, up to and including John. Jesus is come.

teachings.title: The Woman's Seed and the Serpent's Seed
teachings.summary: Revelation 12 fulfils Genesis 3: Eve's seed is Christ who crushes Satan, while Satan's seed are the reprobate who persecute those who overcome by the blood.
teachings.text:
Moving to the second half of Revelation, we take a step back, and in the more symbolic vision of John, we have what is essentially the fulfilment of the Genesis 3 prophecy, Eve, the mother of man, bringing forth her seed, even Jesus Christ, the Son of man.

The enmity of the serpent and the woman, his seed and her own. She bringing forth the man child who will crush Satan's head, he seeking to devour Him as soon as He was born.

The seed of Eve is man, and through her, Jesus. The seed of Satan are his spawn, reprobates. Sons of Belial. Twice-dead dogs. Vipers.

*Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.*

And so Satan tempts the earth and brings against all man tribulation. Going before the throne of God accusing man night and day. And knowing the Christ was born, sought to destroy Him through Herod, killing all the male children.

Ultimately, by the Jews who were Satan's seed, bruising the heel of Jesus, in death, only to see Jesus rise triumphant, overcoming the world with the keys to Hell and Death. And those sons of men who held the testimony of Jesus overcame through the blood of the Lamb.

And so it has been, Satan accusing and tempting the world, he and his wicked seed persecuting those who have overcome by the blood of Christ, and destroying mankind at every opportunity, like a ravenous lion.

But, as the end comes he will be cast out by Michael and his angels, and will be loosed on the earth for a short time to do his worst. This is the Great Tribulation, and for a 3 and a half year period, making war on the saints and overcoming them. But they who love not their lives unto death shall be saved....

teachings.title: God will provide Himself a lamb
teachings.summary: Abraham's offering of Isaac on Moriah pictures Christ in every detail, from the wood carried uphill to the ram in the thorns.
teachings.text:
and it came to pass after these things, God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, behold, *here I am.* (Remember this for later)

Take thy thou only son whom you lovest, take him to the land of Moriah (2 Chronicles 3:1 tells us that Moriah is where Jerusalem is). And offer him there for a burnt offering (Jesus three days and nights in Hell) upon one of the mountains which I will tell the of (Golgotha?)

On the third day, (obvious), Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place a far off. (Jesus lifting up his eyes rising up from hell)

I in the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. (Abraham had no doubt that even if he slay his son that God would resurrect him).

And Abraham took the wood of the burned offering and laid it upon Isaac his son and he took the fire in his hand in a knife and they went both of them together. (Isaac the sacrifice carrying wood up the hill of Golgotha in Jerusalem)

Behold the fire and wood but where is the Lamb for burnt offering? And Abraham said *God will provide himself* a lamb for burnt offering. (God literally is providing himself as the lamb for the burnt offering. That's carefully phrased, don't miss it!)

And Abraham stretch forth with his hand and the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the Lord called unto him out of heaven, and said, abraham, Abraham: and he said *here am I.* (*Here I am* is where you brought yourself. *Here am I*  is a place where you've been brought)

And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad neither do thou anything unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou has not withheld by son, thine only son from me. (Again. Note Isaac isn't Abraham's only son, he has an older son Ishmael, God is being precise for a reason, this is a picture of Jesus)

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns and Abraham went and took the ram and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son. (From the crown of thorns to being the burnt offering in place of Abraham's son, God placed his only begotten son)

teachings.title: Coats of skins: the first promise of Christ
teachings.summary: In Genesis 3 God promises the seed who bruises the serpent's head and covers Adam and Eve with skins by shed blood, a picture of Christ's imputed righteousness.
teachings.text:
So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world.

To the devil, that old serpent, *Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post.  But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ.

To Eve, *I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will.

This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything).

And to man, through Adam, we are punished;

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin.

But here, in **Genesis 3**, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins.

 *Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours.

And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God.

This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God.

 *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Amen

teachings.title: The seed of the woman bruises the serpent's head
