teachings.summary: Revelation 12 fulfils Genesis 3: the devil, cast out, wars against the saints in the great tribulation while Christ, bruised on the heel, comes to crush his head.
teachings.text:
A murderer from the beginning, father of lies, the accuser of man before God in Heaven, with enmity with all of mankind, through Eve.

 Waiting to devour man all men, like a ravenous lion, and to devour Christ as soon as He was born though a child of the devil, Herod.

The devil is finally cast out, a 3rd of the host with him, and they fall. Shut out of Heaven and knowing their time short, they begin the great tribulation, to murder as many of *the remnant of the seed which kept the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus.*

Christ Jesus, the ruler of a rod of iron. Come to establish the Kingdom. Who, as a man on the cross, was bruised on the heel, but in the resurrection came into glory. Come to bruise that old serpent's head.

The three and a half years of great tribulation begin with his fall.

Because he is a murderer who hates mankind, hates Jesus. Hates God. And his seed are those who do too. Reprobates. They will make war with the saved, sons of God. And they will remain faithful unto death, having overcome in the blood of Christ.

It's one story. Genesis to Revelation.

teachings.title: The sign of the prophet Jonas
teachings.summary: The tomb was empty before dawn Sunday after three full days and nights, fulfilling the sign of Jonas, and getting this timing wrong opens the door to worse error about Christ's suffering.
teachings.text:
Now, the first day of the week in the Bible is what we call Sunday. This finishes establishing the timeline of Jesus' death, burial and resurrection. Following 3days and nights, *before* dawn Sunday morning, Mary comes and the tomb is empty, Christ has risen already. The "night" is not yet "over," being yet dark. Wednesday night, Thursday night, Friday night. Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

*But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.*
...
*Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.*
*For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.*
*Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God. When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.*
*They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.*

It's a minor doctrine, the timing of these things, and yet its corruption and basic misunderstanding lead to all kinds of heresy and error. The day of the week isn't really important, but what Jesus did in that time is.

Often false teachers will use misunderstanding and error to build other, more damnable doctrine. Such as Jesus didn't suffer in Hell as a burnt offering for sin. Such as He didn't do so for 3 days and nights as the Bible says, making some doubt scripture.

Nothing in the Bible is incidental, accidental or coincidental. All scripture is valuable for doctrine.

teachings.title: Not a bone of Him broken
teachings.summary: Psalm 34's unbroken bones, fulfilled at the cross and pictured in the Passover lamb, show that all scripture points to Jesus and that God keeps His prophetic promises.
teachings.text:
In addition to the worship and praise of God, the recognition that His burden is light and He rewards us for bearing it, and the comfort that in our suffering and trouble, He is there, working it for good, **Psalm 34** contains a prophetic verse of Christ;

*He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.*

**John 19:31–37**
*The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.*

Nothing in Scripture is incidental, accidental or coincidental. And ultimately, everything points to Jesus.

**Exodus 12:46**
*In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.*

The Passover lamb being a clear type of Christ, the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The instructions repeated again, to emphasize the importance:

**Numbers 9:12**
*They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.*

The picture of Christ given throughout Old Testament scripture shows the power of His word, knowing the end from the beginning.

**1 Corinthians 1:27–29**
*But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

There is no wisdom of this world that can explain the prophetic nature of scripture. It is foolishness to those that reject the truth. Yet the sheer overwhelming number of things which are not that become things that are, shows the glory of God and the folly of man.

 And the faithfulness of prophecy shows us the power of God to keep His promises, and increase our faith. Amen

teachings.title: The priests stood, but Christ sat down
teachings.summary: The priests had no seat because their sacrifices never took away sins, but Christ sat down at God's right hand after one sacrifice forever.
teachings.text:
*Hebrews 10:11*
*And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins*

In the physical Tabernacle and the Temple of Solomon, there were no chairs. A priest could never sit down because his job was never done. The blood of bulls and goats only provided a temporary cover for the *remembrance of sins made again every year*, meaning the priest had to stay on his feet, continuously working, because he could never truly take away sins.

But then we see Jesus, the author and most importantly, the finisher of our faith, sits down, on the right hand of the Father.

**Hebrews 10:12–14**
*But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.*

The contrast of those who stood, continually ministering, versus Jesus, Who sat down forever, having perfected them that are sanctified, is a subtle but crucial detail. An interesting side note to the study, that we shouldn't overlook.

teachings.title: Jerusalem, where God placed His name
teachings.summary: Jerusalem and Mount Moriah, where God chose to place His name and provided the ram for Isaac, point to Christ, the name God placed there to be sacrificed and to reign.
teachings.text:
Jerusalem, was chosen by God to "place His name";

**Deuteronomy 12:5, 11**
*But unto the place which the LORD your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come...Then there shall be a place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there; thither shall ye bring all that I command you; your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which ye vow unto the LORD*

The OT scriptures repeatedly say that Jerusalem is where God chose to place His name. Where the Son of God would be revealed. Where His name would be killed for our transgressions:

**Isaiah 53:3–5**
*He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.*

The same place Abraham was told to bring Isaac, at Mount Moriah, Zion:

**Genesis 22:2**
*And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.*

But God did not require the sacrifice of man, but rather gave His only begotten Son:

**Genesis 22:8**
*And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.*

In this place, where the altar was made, and the son was to be sacrificed, where a ram without blemish was caught in the thick of thorns was provided, Abraham recognized it for what it was:

**Genesis 22:14**
*And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.*

The place where the temple would be, pointing to the Messiah:

**1 Kings 8:28–29**
*Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.*

God says that His promise to David that the anointed one would come from his line, and His determined use of Jerusalem as the city where He would place His name, is the only reason He did not wipe out Judah as He did Israel.

**Isaiah 37:34–35**
*By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

**Zechariah 9:9**
*Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.*

There, in Jerusalem would He place His name, Christ Jesus. The Alpha and Omega. The Lord of lords and King of kings.

**Isaiah 9:6**
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.*

teachings.title: Why Christ died in this manner
teachings.summary: Every sacrifice from Adam onward pictured the Lamb slain, and the cross and resurrection had to happen before witnesses so that all nations could hear the gospel and believe without seeing.
teachings.text:
I recently was giving the gospel to someone who said, "I understand God loves us, and that His Son, Jesus was born and died and rose again for us, but I struggle with the question; Why?" Not as in why did God do this, which we know is because He so loved us. But why in this manner?

I think one of the reasons is that man by our nature we know sin requires a sacrifice for atonement.

Of course every animal sacrificed from Adam and Eve and God showing them the way, through righteous Abel, to Noah disembarking from the ark, to Abraham with Melchizedek, to Moses and Arron and the Levitical priests, were pictures given by God of the actual sacrifice to come. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. And they who trusted in the Christ to come were saved by that faith. But without some means of understanding, it was difficult for them to form faith. Thus the process laid out in the law.

But for the other nations called, after the crucifixion and resurrection, the one sacrifice made for all time, for all sin, by Jesus' blood, man needed to understand it clearly. And so we place trust in His word. Faith being the evidence of things not seen, which comes from hearing His word. There needed to be witnesses. It had to happen here, in this world that others would believe, sight unseen.

As Jesus says to Thomas, *blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.*

Without the prophets and scriptures promising Christ, the sacrifice of Christ, and without the witnesses to the resurrection testifying of Christ, I think man would not believe God wanted to forgive them. Without the gospel preached, a witness, exactly as it stands:

**1 Corinthians 15:1-8**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.*

teachings.title: Christ our Passover, not a wafer
teachings.summary: At Easter he teaches Christ, the Passover lamb, is the bread of life by one finished sacrifice, not a wafer or cup of wine.
teachings.text:
And so we enter into *Pascha*, Easter, the Passover feast in which Christians remember Christ's triumphant entrance to Jerusalem, His final meal with the Apostles, His promise of a new covenant, the cup and the bread offered in remembrance of the sacrifice He would make, His betrayal by Judas, made with a kiss, His being presented before the high priests, a lamb without blemish, offered up as the Passover lamb, slain before the foundation of the world for the remission of sins for all men, especially them that believe. His 3 days and 3 nights in Hell, a burnt offering. His glorious resurrection on the first day of the week, with the keys to Hell and Death. The hope of eternal life given us in Jesus by the grace of God. We should remember that the bread of life is Christ.

Not a cracker. Not a wafer. Not some baked cube of wheat and water. The blood of Christ was shed on that hill in Jerusalem, it isn't in a cup of juice or wine. But we remember His covenant made by his literal blood and body. His blood was sprinkled on the Mercy Seat in Heaven, one time. One sacrifice.

We who eat of this bread, come down from Heaven, and drink of the living waters that flow from Christ, shall never hunger nor thirst again. We are redeemed by that promise. The Word of God made flesh.

Not by the drinking of blood and pollution of idols. Not by meat and drink offerings sacrificed to idols continually, never satisfying, never taking away sin. But by the finished work of Christ Jesus, given by the grace and love of God the Father. Amen

teachings.title: The red heifer fulfilled in Christ
teachings.summary: The red heifer burned with cedar, hyssop and scarlet pictures Christ's sacrifice, not a prophecy needed for a third temple.
teachings.text:
The law of the water of separation is given by the Lord. That those that become unclean by contact with a dead person could be purified, and the things of the tent where in the person died, and their sin be covered, a purification ritual.

The law requires a red heifer, without blemish, be brought without the camp and slain and burned. In the fire was required cedar, hyssop and scarlet. This is a holocaust, a burnt offering, that is an explicit picture of Christ. The cedar wood of the cross, the hyssop dipped in vinegar, the scarlet of His blood.

The ash mixed with water to be used on the 3rd day for purification, that on the 7th day the unclean may be clean. The parallel with Jesus 3 days and nights, and our redemption at his eventual return.

Note, this is not a "prophecy of a red heifer," which has been in the news lately. Where they claim that "Israel" needs a red heifer to build the third temple, a "prophecy" some American cow farmer invented in the 1990s.

Whatever prophecy this ritual foresaw was filled in Christ. The burnt offering for our sin, and the water of life given us to purify ourselves.

teachings.title: Ordinances a memorial of Christ
teachings.summary: The offerings pictured Christ as the Lord's supper memorializes Him, ordinances having no power themselves, and the stranger always had the same salvation by faith.
teachings.text:
**Numbers 15** veers back to the clarification of the law, in this chapter, the ordinances of sacrifice, the meat offerings which includes the lambs or goats, which contain the blood of the testament between God and the Israelites, but also the flour and oil, which is made bread and wine, the juice of the vine.

Just as Jesus is the lamb slain for our sins, and His body broken like bread for our transgressions, and the cup offered as the blood of the new and better testament between God and man.

Ordinances are a memorial. They themselves have no power, and aren't the thing itself, but a picture of that thing, so too are the sacrifices given Moses a picture of Christ to come. Given us, as the Lord's supper, in remembrance of the risen Christ Jesus. That whenever it is done, we memorialize His work and the promise of God, until Jesus returns.

And we see that the stranger among the Israelites would be given the same ordinance, for the same memorial, of the same faith. There is no Jew or Greek.

God is not a respecter of persons. The salvation offered by faith was always available to whosoever will. To those that call upon the name of the Lord. Before there was Abraham. Before the circumcision. Before Jacob birthed Israel. Before the giving of the law at Sinai. The promise of salvation was given to all who called upon the name of the Lord, and they were made sons of God.

Israel was meant to be a beacon, to draw all men to repentance that they could participate in the supper table of the Lamb. But in their failing, God lifted up Jesus that all men be called that some might be saved. Amen.

teachings.title: The Passover open to every stranger
teachings.summary: The Passover pictures salvation in Christ offered to anyone, the unclean and the stranger alike, with those who refuse cut off, and after salvation we follow the Lord.
teachings.text:
We are in **Numbers 9**, and we see this the 3rd Passover, held in the wilderness and the Lord tells Moses not to forget the ordinance that He has established, using the Passover in Egypt and the physical salvation of Israel as a picture of Christ and the individual salvation of man. I've done larger studies on the parallels and processes [before](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9752). But it is always good to note that it was a reminder of Christ to come, just as the Lord's supper is a reminder of Christ for us now.

Here, God provides Moses with a few guidelines given circumstance. That the ceremonially unclean and those sojourning participate in Passover just the same, that strangers among them that wish to are invited, and those that don't participate are cut off and bear their own sin.

The parallels are pretty clear as to how this corresponds to individual salvation in Jesus. Anyone. Even the unclean. Even those afar off from God, get to participate in the sacrifice and the blood. Even the stranger among them. The sinner, the worldly, the Gentile...all are invited to take part in the salvation by the blood, in the faith of Jesus Christ.

And those who don't are cut off and made to pay for their sin.

It is that simple. People try to overcomplicate salvation because they want to make it about themselves or to make it a sensual experience that they can "feel," or see. Because they lack faith, which is the evidence of things unseen.

And then we are called to follow Him.

Just as the movement of the Tabernacle and the camps was dictated by the movement of God upon them, the pillars of smoke and fire. At the commandment of the Lord they moved. At His command they rested.

And so it is to be in our lives, that after salvation we follow the Lord.

teachings.title: The redemption of the firstborn
teachings.summary: The shekels paid for the firstborn beyond the number of Levites picture the price of our redemption, paid by Christ, God's firstborn Son.
teachings.text:
God's original plan for the children of Israel was that their firstborn sons would be given to Him in service to the Lord, and the firstborn cattle as sacrifice, thus a picture of Christ Jesus. But the children of Israel failed almost immediately after being led from Egypt, worshipping the golden calf;

**Exodus 32:25-29**
*And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:) Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour. And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.*

This incident changed the plan, and instead a generational priesthood was created from the Levites, under the charge of Aaron.

And so this left an accounting due the Lord.

Here we see at the poll of men, numbering them by tribe, that the Levites were fewer in number than the firstborn sons of Israel, and so a reckoning was due. And to offset the difference, a collection of 5 shekels was made for each son. God will always receive His due.

The redemption of this time is a picture of the redemption in Christ of believers. The cost, His life and death and blood. The burnt offering of His firstborn Son. And the resurrection the promise made in Him.

There is always a price for redemption. And the price for righteousness is Christ, His imputed righteousness on all who believe.

teachings.title: The camps of Israel and the throne of God
teachings.summary: The four standards of Israel's camps around the tabernacle mirror the four living creatures around God's throne in Ezekiel and Revelation, because the tabernacle was made after the pattern of the things in heaven.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 4:1-9**
*After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald. And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold. And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.*

*And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.*

*And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come. And when those beasts give glory and honour and thanks to him that sat on the throne, who liveth for ever and ever...*

**Ezekiel 1:3-10**
*The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him. And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass. And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward.*

*As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle.*

**Ezekiel 10:14**
*And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.*

**Numbers 2:1-2**
 *And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, Every man of the children of Israel shall pitch by his own standard, with the ensign of their father's house: far off about the tabernacle of the congregation shall they pitch.*

Each camp, Judah, Ruben, Ephraim and Dan had a banner. And each banner, and ensign; also called a symbol or crest.

The camps surrounding the Tabernacle containing the Ark of the Covenant, the throne of God. His mercy seat. The creation of which was a pattern shown Moses, reflecting the things in Heaven.

**Hebrews 8:1-5**
*Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.*

teachings.title: The camp of Israel laid out as a cross
teachings.summary: The tribes camped around the tabernacle likely formed a cross facing east toward Judah, a picture of Christ the morning star.
teachings.text:
Now, to the point. What **Numbers 2** lays out is a picture of the camp, surrounding the Tabernacle, the heart of the camp where the Spirit of God appears as a cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. The Levites to each direction, serving the 4 camps.

The rectangular tent of the Tabernacle facing East would see the camp of Judah. Larger than the others. West, a bit smaller. North and South, almost equal.

There are two schools of thought on this, presented above. One school teaches that each camp surrounded the Tabernacle in a square, the tribes each side by side.

The other sees the camp laid out in a nearly perfect cross. With the camps laid out by one tribe, next to them another, and then another.

A cross with the heart being the holy place of God. Where the blood was shed for sacrifice, a picture of Christ. Facing East, looking towards Judah. Jesus being the morning star.

teachings.title: Balaam looked down on the cross
teachings.summary: Balaam marveling at the tents of Israel was looking upon a camp laid out as a cross, since Numbers is full of pictures of Christ.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 22:16**
*I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.*

While we cannot know with 100% certainty that the layout was a cross, it certainly is what is described in my opinion. I cannot see it any other way, and Numbers has many references to Jesus, as we will see. The idea it would just be an uneven box-shaped camp seems absurd.

Not to get to any spoilers, consider this passage from **Numbers 24;**

*And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him. And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said: He hath said, which heard the words of God, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!*

Balaam, a character we shall encounter soon enough, is looking down at the camp of Israel and the Spirit of God came upon him and he marveled at the layout of the camp.

I don't believe that he was viewing a rough square. I believe he was looking towards the cross.

teachings.title: Four standards and the pattern of heaven
teachings.summary: The four camps may have borne the lion, ox, man and eagle of the cherubim around God's throne, picturing Christ after the heavenly pattern shown Moses.
teachings.text:
*For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.*

**Exodus 25:40**
*And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount*...

The visions and revelations given John and Ezekiel, which show their witness to the things in Heaven, include creatures, Cherubim, with 4 faces; a lion, a calf/ox/cherubim (a cow like face for all three), a man and an eagle, surrounding the throne of God.

Nothing in the Bible is incidental, accidental or coincidental.

Christian tradition has even placed the 4 Gospels as being symbolized by these same figures. In his Commentary on the Gospel of Matthew, Jerome associated each Evangelist with one of the living creatures: Matthew is the Man; Mark is the Lion; Luke is the Calf and John is the Eagle. Of course we know that Jesus is the Lion of Judah.

**Revelation 5:5**
*And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.*

Whe know that the Lion of Judah is opposed by the fallen cherubim, Lucifer, who is worshipped as an idol of a calf, or an oxen-headed furnace to Moloch. Jesus becomes man, and then after His triumph, ascends like an eagle. And at His return, gathers the elect like eagles in the clouds.

Were the 4 banners with their sigils, their ensigns, displaying these symbols? Were each camp represented of some aspect of Christ and the Gospel of God? And thus the pattern of Heaven pictured among the camp of Israel?

The Bible doesn't say. Not definitively.

But this is how it seems to me.

teachings.title: The scapegoat and the sin offering
teachings.summary: On the day of atonement the slain goat pictures Christ and the scapegoat the remission of sins carried away and remembered no more.
teachings.text:
As for the two goats, brought before the Lord and lots cast to determine one to be the sin offering, whose blood was given to take away the sins of the children of Israel, the other made the scapegoat, who would be led to the wilderness and let go.

The lot cast are the **Urim and Thummim**, the means by which God "spoke" through the high priest. The sin offering a picture of Jesus, the scapegoat a picture of the remission of sin, brought away from the congregation and left in the wilderness to be remembered no more.

**Jeremiah 50:20**
*In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.*

The high priest would place his hands upon the head of the scapegoat and confess the sins of the people, that the goat would carry them, *all their* *transgressions in all their sins*.

**Hebrews 8:12**
*For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: The cleansing of the leper points to Christ
teachings.summary: The law for cleansing a cured leper, a seemingly impossible event, is full of pictures of Christ and served as a testimony that a prophet, the Son of God, was among them.
teachings.text:
I have covered the symbolism and importance of the law of leprosy, and the atonement offered at the cleansing of one who is cured in another post [here](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9168).

It is fascinating to me that an incurable disease is given a process by God for ritual cleansing in the case of a leper who is cured.

There were cases in the OT of leprosy being "cured." In **Numbers 12**, after Aaron and Miriam gainsay Moses for marrying an Ethiopian, God curses Miriam with leprosy for 7 days.

The other instance is in **2 Kings** 5, where a captain of the Syrian guard, Naaman contracts the disease, and the Syrian King sends him to the king of Israel asking him to heal his servant.

*And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.*

As we see, it was as if he had asked him to raise the dead. An impossible task and the king worried that it was a provocation for war with Syria. But the prophet Elisha heard of it and said;

*And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.*

It's a wonderful story of faith and shows the power of God, highly recommend reading it.

But we can see that the idea that one could be healed from leprosy would have been something that the Israelites would have thought impossible save by God.

And yet an entire chapter is devoted to this unlikely thing, filled with imagery of the sacrifice of Christ. A picture of Jesus saving sinners from death. And the purpose of the practical application, as we see Elisha say, is to let people know there is a prophet of God among them.

Jesus heals the leper and sends him to the temple to perform this ritual, as a testimony unto the priests, that the Son of God was here.

teachings.title: The bloody sacrifices show the cost of sin
teachings.summary: The gory sin offerings, slain by the sinner's own hand, showed Israel beforehand that the cost of sin is death, fire and blood, fulfilled in Christ's passion.
teachings.text:
Running behind a little bit but luckily for us, the New Testament is the best study guide for the Old.

We see that they sent offerings are given not only by the people but by the priest. And provides an opportunity for those in good conscience who may through ignorance violate the law. But later come to know that they did and seek forgiveness.

This is just as a child is born sinless and until the knowledge of the law comes, until they know right from wrong, send isn't held against them by God. It is only the knowledge of the law that kills us in sin. And it's only from that knowledge that we come to understand we need a savior. As Paul writes in **Romans 7**:

*For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.*

Now again the sacrifices are being given by God to the Hebrews as a sign of the Christ to come. He will fulfill all of the different oblations and propitiations. But we should note how bloody this is. How gory. That the man seeking forgiveness for himself or his immediate family is laying his hand on each sacrifice at the door and slaying it before the Lord.

This is a gruesome reminder of what Christ will go through. We have the entire account of his passion from four gospels and still it's difficult for us to comprehend. Now imagine a people before Christ. Looking forward to the cross. And we see in this way God is showing us exactly how the cost for our sin is death and fire and blood.

teachings.title: The meat offering a picture of Christ
teachings.summary: The unleavened, anointed meat offering pictures sinless Christ, and the salted firstfruits picture the saved, preserved by the Holy Spirit and spared the fire.
teachings.text:
The first several chapters of Leviticus, which lays out the Levitical priesthood and its ordinances and practices, deal with the subject of sacrifice for atonement and oblations, gifts given to the Lord of meats, which in Biblical terms is foodstuffs, not just flesh of an animal.

As we see in chapter 1, this is the holocaust or burnt offering of the lamb without blemish. The blood carrying the atonement. The sweet savour of the fire roasted fats and meats being pleasing to the Lord.

And this is a picture of Christ. Just as are the meat offerings in chapter 2. Everything in the Old Testament does.

Here we see the gift offering of fine flour, anointing oil and frankincense. The bread, representing Jesus, made without leaven, leaven representing sin.  Note that it was both raw ingredients baked by Aaron and his sons. Or finished cakes and wafers. Cooked or baked. And the priests eat thereof what is left over. The frankincense consumed completely, all anointed with oil, as befitting a King.

*And the priest shall take from the meat offering a memorial thereof, and shall burn it upon the altar: it is an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.*

Showing the Israelites the truth of their savior in these ordinances. As a memorial to Him that was to come. All burnt upon the fire.

But the oblations of the firstfruits shall not be burnt in the altar. And all the meat offerings of the first fruits are to be salted generously. To season it completely as it is the salt of the covenant with God.

This represents the saved, the firstfruits of the harvest. The salt, the holy Spirit.

*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men*.

Salt is a seasoning, increasing the savour of the food, enhancing it. But it is also a preservative, keeping food fresh, longer. In this way, the Spirit acts in the believer. It isn't burned in the fire, just as believers are spared Hell.

God makes a provision for the corn given in a meat offering to be as the flour or unleavened bread, anointed with oil and frankincense, to be burned as the other flours, as a cornmeal, that there be no confusion.

teachings.title: The burnt offering: free will and substitution
teachings.summary: The burnt offering was offered by a man's own voluntary will as a substitute for his sin, refuting Calvinism and the Orthodox and Catholic errors on atonement.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 1:3-4**
*If his offering be a burnt sacrifice of the herd, let him offer a male without blemish: he shall offer it of his own voluntary will at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the Lord. And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.*

Just to review something I meant to point out yesterday; note that the burnt offering is both of a man's own free will, and is an offering for substitutionary atonement.

Not a man chosen before time by God. Not some elect men, who are drawn and compelled to offer it. But by his own voluntary will.

And this offering was in his place for the payment of sin. It was the faith in God that held the remission of sin, the blood and the fire that was a picture of that faith, showing the pattern of things in Heaven.

This is yet another blow to Calvanism and to the damnable heresy taught by the Orthodox Church that there is no substitutionary atonement with Christ, and the strange and contradictory attempt by the Roman Catholics to square vicarious penal atonement, which is the Biblical doctrine as we see reflected in Leviticus, and their own existing heresies, mainly from Augustine and his progeny.

Jesus, the lamb without blemish, sacrificed for our sins. A propitiation that takes away the sin of all who voluntarily trust on Him for our salvation.

teachings.title: The half shekel ransom for souls
teachings.summary: The equal half shekel atonement paid by rich and poor was a memorial pointing to Christ, the ransom price paid for all our souls.
teachings.text:
Exodus chapter 30 continues laying out the physical tabernacle and carnal ordinances and diverse washings for Aaron and the priesthood, the incense altar and the holy oils and perfumes for anointing, as well as curses on those who fail to keep God's instructions regarding them, or who profanes the holy things.

We see that it is gold that makes the altar precious, and myrrh and frankincense for the anointing oil and holy perfume; a picture of the gifts given Christ by the three wise men and His holy being.

But God takes a slight detour from the ordinances of Aaron and his sons, to an offering given among the people. That when the people are numbered, an offering of half a shekel be given for every, on top of tithes, as an atonement offering. A ransom for their souls. Everybody paying the same price. No more no less, rich or poor. That it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel before the Lord.

This requirement being a memorial, through the generations to come across the centuries, pointing to the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh to be the actual ransom for all. A picture of the price paid for the atonement of our souls.

*For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.*

Amen

teachings.title: Blue, purple and scarlet
teachings.summary: Every detail of the tabernacle, from its colours to the veil torn at Christ's death, points to Christ and is not irrelevant to the believer.
teachings.text:
Blue, purple and scarlet, the so-called royal colors, were key to the design of the Tabernacle and come up frequently in the building of the Temples. The colors of the bruises and blood of Christ, by which we are healed.

The instructions for building the Tabernacle, the layers of curtains or walls of the tent, from the dainty fine linen cunningly stitched to the rugged, inside and out. The qualities of a man. The holy of holies at its heart. The law of God and His promise kept there in the Ark. Behind the veil. The veil which tore in twain at the death of Jesus, the separation from God and man done away with.

Everything in the Old Testament is pointing to Christ. including this. It may seem like an Ikea assembly manual and in the view of modern theologies that strip Christ from the "Jewish Bible," the Old Testament becomes meaningless and seems irrelevant to the believer. But every aspect matters. Every detail. Even the color and size and shape.

teachings.title: The tabernacle, a pattern of heavenly things
teachings.summary: Every part of the tabernacle is a picture of Christ and the Christian life: the freewill offering of accepting the gospel, the ark as the covenant written on our hearts, the shewbread as God's word, and the candlestick as the light of Christ.
teachings.text:
Transitioning from the previous chapters where the law of the covenant was given to the children of Israel and accepted in the blood of Moses sacrifices, God begins to instruct on the ceremonial ordinances, specific the building of the Tabernacle. The tent dwelling of God among His people.

It is important to understand that everything in this is a picture of Christ and the spiritual application is of Christianity.

**Hebrews 9**
*23 It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

*24 For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:*

The sanctuary, or holy place made with human hands represents the spiritual.

God says take the free will offering of the people to build with. They have to willingly offer to build the sanctuary. Our free will acceptance of the Gospel.

Then, God starts His instruction with the Arl of the Covenant, which will be kept in the heart of the Tabernacle. Where His angels protect His word, the stone tablets of the law, which are now written on our hearts.

**Hebrews 10:16**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them*

And so here we see that this is where the covenant is kept; in our hearts, just as the Ark containing the old covenant was kept in the heart of the Tabernacle.

We see that it is the mercy seat, the seat of judgment of God, overseen by His angels, just as we as believers are.

**Hebrews 8:5**
*Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.*

Next God instructs that a table be made before the Ark, and on it the shewbread, bread left daily in the Tabernacle and temple. The daily bread, which is God's word.

**Deuteronomy 8:3**
*And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.*

Then the candlestick, with the 7 candle holders, a picture of the light of Christ. The light of life. The 7 candles, the 7 spirits of God.

**John 8:12**
*Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.*

Jesus has the 7 spirits of God; the Spirit of the Lord, and the Spirits of wisdom, of understanding, of counsel, of might, of knowledge and of fear of the LORD.

And God says again; *And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.*

teachings.title: The passover lamb and the Lord's supper
teachings.summary: The Passover ordinance pictured Christ the Lamb, and at His last supper Jesus turned it into a new memorial ordinance, the Lord's supper, done in remembrance of Him.
teachings.text:
We find Jesus, now just one day from His crucifixion, very desirous to eat the passover. He mentions this desire repeatedly, telling His disciples to go and find such and such room, and prepare *where I shall eat the passover with my disciples.*

This is the first of the holy days of the year, which begins in spring in the Hebrew calendar, the first month *Adar*.
10 days in, the lamb without blemish is brought before the people, separated from the flock. On the 14th day the lamb is slain before the congregation. The blood spread with hyssop upon the wooden door posts, in remembrance of the first passover where this saved those within the home from the angel of death, given as an ordinance by God that in future generations when asked by those children, *What mean ye by this service?*  That they would explain the sacrifice, what it meant, and how God delivered the people with the blood of the lamb. That they cast out the leaven of their households, and broke and ate unleavened bread in remembrance of their flight from Egypt.

And ordinance is a memorial service, a ritual that is designed as a picture of something, to be kept as a reminder to future generations so they would understand.

*And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.*

God essentially saying, "Do this in memory of Me."

Jesus, intent to have this passover supper, before His betrayal and death, brings the disciples together, and immediately turns from the traditional Passover ordinance, the ritual observance with unleavened bread, the unfermented juice of the vine and the lamb, and gives unto them a new ordinance; what we call the Lord's supper.

Jesus being the lamb to be delivered to the high priests to be slaughtered. His body broken as the unleavened bread is broken. The cup of the fruit of the vine poured out, and divided, as His blood. Blood put upon the doorways of our hearts that we be saved from death. That it passover us.

The passover observance being a picture of Christ's death. The feast of unleavened bread, the forgiveness of sin. Being brought out of Egypt and to the promised land, a picture of our deliverance to the Kingdom of God.

This, Jesus last meal before betrayal, and in it He provides a new ordinance to be done in His memory, that when future generations may ask, *What mean ye by this service?* We have a ready answer.

The cup is the new testament in Jesus' blood, which is shed for us. The bread, His body that was broken upon the cross. We do this in memory of Jesus.

teachings.title: The leper's cleansing birds a picture of Christ
teachings.summary: The Leviticus 14 ritual for a cleansed leper, with the slain bird in an earthen vessel and the living bird released, is a detailed picture of Christ's death and resurrection.
teachings.text:
Next Luke gives us an example of the healing that is a theme of his gospel, being a physician, in this the healing of a leaper who shows great faith and humility "*Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean."* Again, a picture of the manner in which we are saved. Calling upon the mercy of the Lord to make us clean, with the faith to know He is able to.

Jesus heals him, and cautions him to keep the manner of it to himself, but to go to the temple and offer the sacrifice for cleansing from leprosy given of Moses, found in **Leviticus 14**.

It is a complicated ritual, one that must have seen little use in the times it was given in the law, as leprosy is untreatable and the healing from it coming only from a miracle. Yet Moses in the Spirit gives the process in the law, with specificity. I quoted only the first part of the ceremonial sacrifices, but it takes up basically an entire chapter. But nothing in the Bible is accidental, coincidental or incidental.

First the leper goes to the preists who will send one out of the camp, out to the wilderness, to check the man and confirm they are healed. A testimony given, as Jesus says here.

Then the priest must take two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop, and place one of the birds in an earthen vessel, and kill it, sprinkling the blood of the dead bird on the living bird, the wood, the scarlet cloth and the hyssop, and then sprinkle the blood from these items and the living bird on the healed man, 7 times, proclaiming him clean, and releasing the second bird to the wild.

The bird in the earthen vessel, the clay that man is made from, as a substitutionary sacrifice, its blood upon wood, like the wood of the cross. On the scarlet, as the garments of Christ were so stained. On the hyssop, like the sprig dipped in vinegar, given to Jesus on the cross. And this blood of atonement then cleanses the man, and the living bird, like the risen Christ ascends to the heavens.

The other sacrifices require lambs without blemish, etc, and are equally pictures of Christ Jesus. It's a fascinating chapter to read and study on. Placed in the OT that a testimony of Jesus could be made when he healed this man.

teachings.title: The cleansing birds, cedar, scarlet and hyssop
teachings.summary: Isaac's offering and the Leviticus 14 cleansing ritual both picture Christ, showing all the law pointed to Him.
teachings.text:
Of course the sacrifice of Christ Jesus recalls **Genesis 22**, Abraham and Isaac; the purification sacrifice laid out in [Leviticus 14](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/1949), the mount in Jerusalem being where Abraham brought his son. Issac who carried the wood up the hill, to be the burnt offering. God providing the ram, caught by the head in a thicket of thorns.

We see God tell Moses 8n Leviticus that the sacrifice for him that is to be cleansed *two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.*

We see the wood of the cross, the scarlet of the blood, and the hyssop, the same used by the Roman guard to give Jesus the vinegar to drink.

We see one bird placed in an earthen vessel, as Jesus was placed in flesh. We see it sacrificed and burned, its blood put on the living bird, which is then set free.

Everything points to Jesus and everything in the law was a picture of Him to come, so that the Jews would have no excuse.

teachings.title: Forget thy father's house: the bride of the King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45 pictures believers as the bride of Christ, called to love Him above family and nation as a wife leaves her parents, and to look not to earthly lineage but to the spiritual children they win to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 45**, the messianic wedding song, we transition from the King to the bride.

At His right hand stands the queen, decked in gold from Ophir, (a site somewhere south-southwest of Jerusalem renown for its gold).

Her ornamental beauty, provided by the King, to set apart the bride. The honorable women, the church.

As a picture of believers, we see the Kings great desire for the beauty He has bestowed. He is truly Lord and we worship Him.

*Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house*

We are called to hear the appeal from Heaven, to consider and incline our ear (*faith cometh by hearing*), to forget our people and our parents, and to become His.

**Luke 14:26–27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

We are called out, to be His above our family or national bonds. To "hate" here doesn't mean to dislike intensely, as it does today. It means to not love as much, to not prefer over another. To love Christ more than even your kin.

**Matthew 10:35–37**
*For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.*

Just as a wife is called to separate from her parents and cleave unto the husband.

**Genesis 2:24**
*Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.*

Becoming the bride of Christ, cleaving unto Him, placing our love for Him above others. A wedding is a picture of this relationship that we have. It is given as a parable, that we may better know Him.

In our status as His, the great of every nation shall show us favor. Perhaps in the Millennial Kingdom, certainly not in this life. But when we have come into the inheritance, they will respect our rule because Jesus is their Lord, and we are His.

We are arrayed as a burden in gold and fine embroidery, the white garments of purity, the righteousness of Christ that covers us.

*With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king’s palace*

**Luke 15:10**
*Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.*

This is the celebration of salvation. And the future wedding supper we are called to.

*Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.*

We will not look to our earthly heritage, the genealogies and lineage, but instead at those we have won to the Gospel, as children who rule and reign with Christ. It is our godly heritage, the spiritual children we present to Christ.

Looking forward to the future of those we have helped come to repentance. This is our vow to our Lord and Savior.

*I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever*. Amen

teachings.title: Psalm 45 and the conquering King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45, inspired by the Holy Ghost, prophesies Christ the bridegroom King whose truth, meekness and righteousness are the qualities believers should pursue.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 45** is a doctrine-rich wedding song, that speaks clearly of the Lord Jesus, a bride brought to Him, and the promise of exaltation for the King of Kings.

Of course, the dual nature is both a historic royal wedding song and a profound Messianic prophecy, the Psalms often capture both layers in a way that makes them relevant to our lives as believers. It is a testimony to their divine inspiration.

The same inspiration described in the introduction found in verse 1.

The author says his heart is inditing a good matter, meaning fit to burst with the understanding he is speaking of. His *tongue is the pen of a ready writer.*

God has given him the idea, the words, His inspired, God breathed need to speak and record the word of God, that is bubbling our of his heart.

Jesus said *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh*, be it the evil of the Pharisees or the inspired word. Whether the penman, or those who have committed the word to our hearts.

**2 Peter 1:21**
*For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

And so, moved by the Holy Ghost, given the word of God, the ready writer gives us a song of romance and prophecy. Deeply layered and rich, as only scripture can be.

A similar song to Solomon's, messianic prophecy couched in a romantic allusion.

Verse 2 begins the description of One, fairer than all men, full of grace, blessed forever by God. The Christ. His chosen. The groom, and King.

Girded with His sword, the most mighty. Almighty. A name of God given this person. All glory and majesty are His.

Riding majestically, and prosperously, upon a horse to battle.

**Revelation 19:11-13**
*And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God*.

He has the word of God proceeding from His lips. Destroying the enemies of God with His sharp sword. The strength of His right hand, teaching *thee terrible things*.

What a picture that's painted. What a powerful, Almighty Son of God. Who comes to smite the enemies of His Father, and rule with a rod of iron, but His prosperity is in His truth and meekness and righteousness.

The terrible things, are in this context, the fearful lessons of the Lord. And these are grounded in those three qualities. The truth of the word, the meekness of our Savior, His righteousness in all things.

For the Christian, these three qualities are what we should pursue. We should gird ourselves with the sword of Truth, knowing His word in our hearts, ready to deliver it.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Living in meekness, a servant. Condescending to men of low estate, that they may be saved. Putting our heart to The afflicted, the widow, the fatherless, the poor. For the meek shall inherit the Earth.

And living in righteousness. Doing right things by the judgment of God found in His word. Cleansed by the blood and carrying the righteousness of Christ within us. Being holy, as He is holy.

*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

Truth, meekness and righteousness means loving what is good and hating wickedness. This is the inheritance of the Lord and the perfection of it found in Christ Jesus.

**Hebrews 1:8–9**
*But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

teachings.title: Set me as a seal upon thine heart
teachings.summary: The seal on the heart pictures the unbreakable seal of the Spirit, and love that cannot be bought shows God's grace is unmerited, not purchased by works.
teachings.text:
We are in the final chapter of the Song of Solomon, and the opening verses are the woman, longing to openly display affection for her beloved, the way a sister and brother as family could, without being despised. Without the judgment that would come for a maiden to kiss and embrace a lover, even betrothed, in public.

We seem to have come full circle to the beginning of the song. The wedding hasn't happened, the separation and then regained relationship. It is as if she's been dreaming the experience from courtship to maturity, as told in chapters 2-7.

There are repeated stanzas, ideas and the chorus again in verse 4;

 *I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.*

The longing to be with him, and to experience his love, to be in his embrace, echos her plaintive desires in the first few chapters.

But here, after charging the daughters of Jerusalem again, they sing;

*Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved?*

They see the love-changed woman, who was the girl they had watched grow.

The woman professes her love;

*Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.*

The eternal and unbreakable seal of the Spirit, set upon our hearts, once we know Him and are known of Him.

The love of Christ is like an unquenchable fire, the floods cannot drown it. Noah found grace in the eyes of God. His love for man endured, despite *the* flood.

The love of God could not be purchased, even if a rich man sold all his substance for love, he would be despised. It is not found in riches and cannot be bought by our works. It is unmerited. Freely given.

The woman's brothers join the choir, seeing their sister still as the immature girl they have known. Wondering what they shall do for her now, at her betrothal. A reality that big brothers and parents face, when their daughter has matured.

They contemplate what they'd do metaphorically, if she were a foundational wall or a door in need of a frame. But she states that she is fully grown. She is a wall and the breasts of her maturity are towers. An allegory for the maturity to come to the Lord, and find His grace.

teachings.title: The vineyard let out to keepers
teachings.summary: Where Israel's husbandmen betrayed the Lord's vineyard, the bride freely gives Him its fruit and pays the keepers, as believers support pastors and missionaries with tithes and offerings.
teachings.text:
Then a parable of her beloved, the lord Solomon, and his vineyard. He let, or leased it out to keepers, to be dressed. And their charge was a thousand pieces of silver, purchased by the fruit they would harvest.

The same is the vineyards of Christ's parables. The talents of silver. The harvest and the increase. The unprofitable servants of Israel, the wicked keepers who slew the prophets and even the Son of the Lord. The spiritual understanding that comes from knowing this first; the Lord planted a vineyard;

**Isaiah 5:1–7**
*Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill: And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes. And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.*

The woman offers her vineyard to Solomon, pledging the tribute of a thousand, and even the keepers, a wage of two hundred. Pledging her fruit to her Lord.

The Lord planted and cultivated a vineyard with Israel, and the husband men betrayed Him. But the woman, as the faithful believer willingly offers herself as a vineyard, and freely gives the Lord His tribute. The fruit we gather. The works we do for the cause of the gospel. She gladly pays the workers a wage. Just as we do with tithes and offerings to sustain our pastors, our churches, ministries and missionaries, that work in the fields for God.

teachings.title: Our testimony in persecution leads others to seek Him
teachings.summary: The daughters who asked what made her beloved special now seek him with her, showing that a believer's faithful testimony through trials leads others to Christ.
teachings.text:
The daughters of Jerusalem chorus in chapter 5 asked of the woman; *What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women?*

The chapter ends with the woman, battered and bloody from the world's treatment of her for his sake, extolling his virtues and singing praise to his perfection.

The character arc from the ecstatic bride at the feast to the complacent woman, making excuses to avoid her love, then realizing and searching him out again, only to be mistreated by the watchmen and questioned by the daughters, and ultimately to still profess her love and devotion for Jesus, is a wonderful picture of things that can and do happen in the Christian life.

And her faith through the trials leads others to seek Him.

Chapter 6 opens with the same chorus of daughters, and they have changed their tune.

*Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.*

Our testimony, especially in persecution, not only reestablishes our faith, but leads others to seek Jesus.

We can often feel adrift. We may realize we should do more for the cause of Christ. We may have a sense of separation from Him. We may call out in prayer as David did:

**Psalms 51:12**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.*

But we should be aware that as saved Christians, seeking to get back on the right path, we will see persecution. The devil will attempt to sift us like wheat. Satan doesn't need much to keep the unsaved from seeking truth, but he works overtime to keep Christians from being fruitful.

So, having persuaded the daughters, the woman answers them; that she knows where her beloved has gone. He is down in His garden, to feed the garden and gather lilies. A picture of the gospel light, the harvest of believers, the fruit of His good pleasure.

She affirms her faith; *I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilie*s, and then the narrator shifts again to the King.

He praises his beloved, comparing her beauty to Tirzah, a city known for its natural beauty, and even as Jerusalem, ready for war, filled with bannermen, armies ready to march.

He is overwhelmed with her beauty, repeating the verses poetically comparing her hair and teeth to goats and sheep as the lyrics from chapter 4.

He numbers her among 60 queens and 80 concubines and countless virgins, a royal harem, and says she alone is above them all. Undefiled. The choice daughter, whom all the other women blessed and praised. Beloved above them all.

Verse 10, the daughters of Jerusalem, the very courtesans the King compared his beloved to, sing her praises.

*Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?*

We are His beloved. We are the light of the world. We shine forth to all nations, calling them to Christ. Provoking them to envy, that they may seek to be His bride.

The woman sings in verse 11, that she has gone down to her beloved's garden. To see the fruit of the garden, and if the vine flourished, Jesus is the true vine. She's returned to His rest, as quickly as the chariots, to her beloved, upon seeing the bounty of his garden.

The daughters encourage her, *Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee.* And her beloved asks them *What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.* A refrain answered in the next chapter.

teachings.title: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
teachings.summary: The suffering bride's praise of her beloved describes Christ, divine and human, and her testimony under persecution moves others to ask why He is above all.
teachings.text:
The daughters of Jerusalem answer her refrain;

*What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?*

She has been backslidden, treated horribly by the authorities, bloody, aiming to destroy her remaining faith and strip away her public testimony (the veil), and yet her love is true.

The daughters cannot understand what makes her beloved so special, above all others, that she would still call to him after all she's suffered.

Unsaved people who see Christians suffer for Christ and still preach His love, often are baffled, but sometimes are moved. When the churches have been persecuted, traditionally we have seen exponential growth. Men are persuaded to willingly go to their death for the cause of Christ, and this testimony brings others to the faith.

Why is your beloved more than others? Why is your God over the gods of men?

And she answers.

He is white, with purity, sinless. Divine. Ruddy, a red complexion picturing the humanity of Jesus and blood shed for us. The chiefest among ten those, the Lord of hosts. King of kings.

Crowned of gold, sovereign above all. His locks, eternally young, everlasting. His eyes, full of grace and compassion for His beloved.

Kissing His cheeks, like a bed of spices. Sweet flowers. His kiss, soft like the petals of the lily, dripping with precious oils. His love and our love for Him.

The strength of His hands, the purity of His works, the gold and precious stones of all that He does. The inward parts of Christ are strong and pure as ivory, with heavenly blue sapphires the eternal Godhead in Him.

His legs, a picture of Jesus' unmoving and unswerving strength. He supports us and His ways are golden. Pure. His face, chiseled as the great cedars. His mouth is sweet, all that He says is true.

*This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem*. Oh what a friend we have in Jesus!

teachings.title: The King's wedding procession and many crowns
teachings.summary: The bride's search pictures the empty tomb and finding Christ, and Solomon's procession pictures Christ returning with His saints for the marriage supper and His kingdom.
teachings.text:
Chapter 3 begins with the woman waking to a desolate bed, unable to find her beloved. Seeking him, she desperately searches in the night, throughout the city streets. She repeats the refrain that she *sought him, but I found him not.*

She then encounters the night watch, and enquires of them if they had seen *him, whom my soul loveth.*

This passage beautifully reflects the death of Christ, picturing the panicked feeling of believers at His death, and at the empty tomb. The watchmen, the religious leaders who crucified Him, unable to give an answer, but then, in her search, she finds him. *Him whom my soul loveth.*

And she holds him and will not let him go, bringing him into her mother's house, even to the bed chamber she was conceived in. As Jesus comes into us, and is held in the most intimate chamber of our hearts.

For the second time in the song, the chorus in verse 5, also found in chapter 2:7 is repeated:

*I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please*.

It is repeated again in chapter 8, and the verse is used as transition in the structure of the song.

While it may picture the current time, where we wait for our beloved, the Lord Jesus to return, it also serves as an oath, asking the daughters of Jerusalem to swear by the roes and hinds, the graceful and skittish deer of the land, to not stir the Beloved too early. To let him sleep as late as he pleases.

The immediate application speaks to the delicate nature of love, especially in its earliest stages, where you almost feel a surreal and magical experience and are afraid it could burst like a bubble at any time. You don't want to lose that joyous state. You don't want it to be disturbed, like the gazelles of the mountains startled at a sudden movement or sound.

She has found her beloved and taken him into her heart, and wants that joy of her salvation to last.

The chorus serves to transition the narrative to an epic description of the King, and his entourage, emerging from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, an endless caravan. Perfumed and decked out in fine clothes for the wedding.

This pictures the return of Christ, after the wrath, on a white horse with ten thousands of His saints, wearing their wedding clothes, prepared for the marriage supper of the Lamb.

The bed of the King, his chariot, surrounded by threescore valiant men, the valiant of Israel. The soldiers with swords at their hip, like the prophets armed with the word of God.

King Solomon's chariot, made of the finest wood, decked in silver and gold, covered in royal purple, and as it goes, *paved with love*, *for the daughters of Jerusalem*. This is the interior of the royal chariot, embroidery made by the daughters of the land with love, the inner bed, where the King and his bride would recline.

The purity of God in the silver pillars, His grace, the gold that surrounds us. The purple of His majesty as Lord, and the interior, the soft comfort of His love for us.

The bride of the song calls out for the daughters of Zion, Jerusalem, to go out and welcome the King. To examine his wedding crown, to celebrate the betrothal and his gladness. The tradition of the people is that the mother of the bridegroom crafts a crown to celebrate the nuptials. Not a crown of royalty, but of love.

In **Revelation 19:12**, as Christ rides forth to claim ultimate victory and gather His people, the text says, *on his head were many crowns*.

The crowns of Christ at His triumphant arrival to meet the descending New Jerusalem, adorned as a bride, are the diadem of His love for His beloved, just as Solomon's love for his bride.

As John writes in *Revelation 21:2*:
*And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.*

The allegory and picture of the King of Kings arriving at His wedding feast, at the culmination of history, to usher in His millennial Kingdom, reflected in the prophetic love song written by Solomon.

teachings.title: Rise up, my love, and come away
teachings.summary: The bride waiting for her beloved pictures believers waiting for Christ's return to gather His elect, while the wicked hide in the rocks from the wrath of the Lamb.
teachings.text:
Chapter 2 contains a poetic back and forth dialogue between the woman and the man, the rose of Sharon and her beloved, an apple tree among the trees of the wood. He compares other women to thorns, but she is a lily, a beautiful flower among them.

The woman delights in his shade, his protection, and in his fruit, which is sweet to her taste. He calls her to his banquet, under the banner of love.

Again, we see the gospel. He is the tree of life, over a precious flower among the thorns. Invited to the banquet house of the Lord. The wedding supper of the Lamb.

She is overcome by his love, she longs for him as we long for Jesus, and His embrace in that great day of redemption.

 *I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.*

The timing of the Lord's return is at God's pleasure. Just as she waits for her love to awake, we patiently wait for Him to return.

The roes, the hinds of the field are the wild deer that play in the pastures and roam the hills and mountains.

She hears the voice of her beloved, and compares him to the roebuck leaping and skipping on mountains and hills. She sees him through the lattice of the window, just beyond her walls, and he speaks to her, calling her to rise up and come with him.
