(From the crown of thorns to being the burnt offering in place of Abraham's son, God placed his only begotten son)

The name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen. (And it was amen)

teachings.title: To your tents, O Israel
teachings.summary: Israel's rebellion against Rehoboam in 1 Kings 12 pictures the Jews rejecting Christ, and every man going to his own house in John 7 is its parallel.
teachings.text:
Every man went to his own house, the matter unresolved, reminds me of the verse in **1 Kings 12:16**:

*So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.*

In this account of the old kingdom being divided, between the northern tribes and Judah we see the people demanding that Solomon's son, Rehoboam who has just been anointed king, ease the enforcement of God's law, claiming it's too heavy a yoke to bear. They rebel, they kill the man sent by Rehoboam to collect tribute (picturing God the Father sending Jesus, and the Jews killing Him). They then name Jeroboam their king, (picturing men putting their faith in what they want, rather than what God tells us).

*So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.*..

This rejection led to God's wrath upon the northern kingdom, and their having renounced their inheritance, their portion of the promise in David, they were eradicated by the Assyrians.

This is a picture of the Jews in Jesus' day, some choosing to follow God's anointed, most choosing their own way, and thus divided, each returns to their own house to do as they will.

*O Israel, return to thy tents*, and *every man went unto his own house,* shows that this is a parallel passage.

teachings.title: The three feasts pictured Jesus
teachings.summary: He teaches the pilgrimage feasts picture Jesus and set up His return to Jerusalem at Passover and the gathering at Pentecost, as His children will be gathered at His return.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 16** opens with a recitation of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals, the ordinances set forth by God in the wilderness.

*Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose*

The first Passover and the feast of unleavened bread, then the Feast of Weeks, known as Pentecost, and finally the fall feast of the Tabernacle. While there are details as to their keeping of the feasts, the primary reason for their retelling here, as in previous chapters regarding the sacrifices and such, were to let the Israelites know that they were to go to the place He would designate. The place the Lord would put His name.

These feasts being a picture of Jesus, and the mandate to return to the place God elected to set up His Tabernacle or Temple, set up events in the Gospels. There was a purpose to Jesus of Nazareth returning to Jerusalem for Passover, and the Jews gathered there, just as on Pentecost there were Jews from all over the world returned to mark the feast. Just as at the return of Christ, there will be a gathering of His children.

*And thou shalt rejoice in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy manservant, and thy maidservant, and the Levite, the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within thy gates.*

teachings.title: The sabbath rest and spring feasts picture Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath rest pictures salvation by Christ's finished work rather than ours, and the spring feasts were fulfilled in Christ's death, resurrection and Pentecost.
teachings.text:
Now we are here in Leviticus chapter 23, and in it God provides the basic terms of the sabbaths and holy days to be kept by the children of Israel.

Understanding that sabbaths means rest, and that the prohibition of doing work on the sabbath is a picture of Christ Jesus, and the rest we enter into in Him. That we are saved by the rest given to us by the Lord and not our own works. That if a child of Israel works on these days, he is cut off, just as anyone trusting in their works for salvation is likewise cut off from the Kingdom of God. It is an undeniable truth that is repeated over and over again throughout the Bible, from the creation through Revelation. We are saved by Christ's perfect work, not our own. Not by being a "good person" or contrite or "trying to avoid sin" or how well we make "Jesus the Lord of our life."

Jesus paid it all in full, and the Spring feasts of Passover, unleavened bread and Pentecost all serve as ordinances to the Isralites as a picture of Christ.

I covered much of this in the Gospel studies, recently in [a study of Luke](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/9753).

It is fascinating and amazing how God set this before the people and thousands of years later, we see it pay off with Jesus, the Passover lamb, slain on a sabbath, in Hell for 3 days and nights, all sabbaths, and risen again, only to ascend into Heaven on Pentecost, the feast of the first fruits held 50 days after Passover. The day in which the disciples went out to the multitude of gathered Jews preaching the Gospel in every tongue. The 5,000 saved that day being the first fruits of the spring harvest.

teachings.title: The Fall Feasts Picture the Second Coming
teachings.summary: The fall feasts of Leviticus 23 picture Christ's second coming, and their commanded rest from all work pictures salvation by grace without works.
teachings.text:
The Levitical feasts are also important to understand for our study of Revelation going forward. They are a picture of Christ. Last Easter I gave a rundown of the ways Jesus fufifiled the spring feasts, Passover, the feast of unleavened bread and Pentecost. These were a picture of His first coming. Likewise, the fall feasts God commands in **Leviticus 23** represent Christ at His second coming. The timing, the harvest, the gathering. The blowing of trumpets. The dwelling in houses made by God, while singing His praises. All point to end times Bible prophecy. ("Booths" were tabernacles, tents, made from branches and boughs, rough cut and gathered from nature). The timing of things mirrors events in Revelation, as we will see.

One incredibly important point of the feasts, these Sabbaths; NO WORK was to be done by the people. This is the reinforcement by God of His grace in giving us a free gift of salvation in Jesus, who is the Sabbath. Three days of no works, 3 Sabbaths in a row, from His crucifixion to His resurrection, Jesus doing all the work. And like the Spring feasts, the convocations or gathering of the congregation/church, there is no work allowed, for Jesus did it all.

*For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.*
*And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people.*

These are those unsaved who are appointed to wrath. Notice it is both the unbelieving, those not afflicted by the atonement made by the sacrifice, and those who do any work who are cast out and destroyed. So too will it be in the second coming.

We should all be familiar with **Matthew 7:21-23**:
*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**Romans 4:6-8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

**Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.*

teachings.title: Pentecost: the firstfruits of the harvest
teachings.summary: The feast of weeks was the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, fulfilled when three thousand were saved at Pentecost.
teachings.text:
Fun Fact regarding Pentecost:

The High Holy day, called the Festival of Weeks or "Shavuot," is 7 weeks following the second day of Passover (feast of unleavened bread). In Greek, Pentecost, meaning 50 days following Passover itself.

 Passover commemorates God freeing the Israelites from Egypt, Pentecost, the Feast of Weeks celebrates the day of the giving of the law by Moses and commitment of the people to agree to God's covenant and be His people, detailed in **Exodus 34.**

In the midst of chapter 34, almost as an afterthought, we find verse 22:
*And thou shalt observe the feast of weeks, of the firstfruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of ingathering at the year's end.*

As we know, at Pentecost in Acts, the Apostles and disciples receive gifts of the Holy Ghost, and begin preaching to the multitudes gathered in Jerusalem for the feast, and bring 3000 thousand to salvation.

Literally the first fruits of the harvest.

What an amazing God we have. What a blessing His word is.

teachings.title: Christ our Passover on the preparation day
teachings.summary: Jesus died on Passover preparation day, Wednesday, as the lamb without blemish, and the three Sabbaths that followed picture His doing all the work, the same faith in the blood that saved since Adam.
teachings.text:
Now again, we have the timing of things from John. This is the preparation day for Passover. It is the 6th day since Jesus supper with Mary and Lazarus, 5th day from the triumphant ride into Jerusalem on the weekly Sabbath, Saturday. This is the Wednesday of their week, Passover, a high Sabbath begins at 6pm. This aligns with the first Passover which was a picture of the Christ to come. The lamb chosen without blemish, brought before the high priest on the preparation day. Slaughtered and burned in a fire, a holocaust or burnt offering. His blood what saves those of us cloaked in it.

Passover day is followed by the high holy Sabbath of the feast of unleavened bread, Friday. Saturday is the weekly Sabbath. Three days without work, as Jesus does it all, we can do nothing. Healing us during Sabbath, just as He did so many times to the blind and lame during His ministry. It is why 3 days and 3 nights He will spend dead, in Hell, paying it all for our sin. This is the New Testament.

This is why these days were set by God in the Old Testament. This is the greatest of prophecy fulfilled. And the faith that saved in the Old Testament, the faith that saved since Adam, is in the blood of the lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

It's a beautiful picture of Jesus and the Gospel, of faith without works, of the same dispensation of salvation for all man's history. And so it's no wonder corrupt false churches teach none of it by their calendar.

teachings.title: The feasts of the LORD, Passover and the word Easter
teachings.summary: Shows the spring feasts as a picture of Christ's first coming and defends the KJV's use of Easter in Acts 12 against claims that Christian celebration is pagan.
teachings.text:
The Lord God gave Israel Spring feasts and Fall feasts; that served as a picture of Christ. 

Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, now called Easter, the Feast of First Fruits, and the Feast of Weeks also called Pentecost, were given as a picture of Christ's first coming. 

The LORD'S feast mirroring the Lord's last supper. The Passover lamb, Christ's sacrifice. The purging of the leaven, the remission of sin. First Fruits, Jesus' resurrection.The Feast of Weeks, Pentecost is known as the Feast of Harvest or the Latter Firstfruits, the day the gospel was preached and 3,000 believed on Christ and took that truth to the ends of the earth, an offering to the Lord. 

**1 Corinthians 5:7**
*Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us*.

**1 Corinthians 15:20**
*But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.

***Leviticus 23:9-12***
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest: And he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it. And ye shall offer that day when ye wave the sheaf an he lamb without blemish of the first year for a burnt offering unto the Lord.
*
Similarly, the Fall feasts, or the Harvest feasts; The Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Tabernacles, given in **Leviticus 23**, all point to the Day of the Lord, the judgment and the rapture. Jesus' second coming, which throughout the Bible is compared to agricultural terms. Harvests. Bringing in the sheaves. The fruit of believers, after their own kind. The increase going to the Lord. 

Amen. 

These feasts and days were given of the Lord to us that we may better understand His word, the fulfillment of His promises in the Spring, a time of rebirth, and the prophetic second coming of the end times.

People get caught up in nonsense peddled by some that seek to subvert the faith of many. Vain jangling. And one of the most pernicious is the idea that since pagans had spring and fall feasts, early Christians must have been corrupted by them into adopting them, and so if we mark the occasions in service to the Lord, we are partaking in pagan rituals. 

This is wicked as Hell. 

Pagans had spring and fall feasts because Satan cannot create, only copy. His pale imitations of the feasts God uses as a parable for His people, were taken from us. Not the other way around. 

The Lord Christ Jesus is risen. The final harvest awaits. Let us come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

There is an argument between some KJVOers and those who seek to push false Bible versions and sow doubtful disputations, about the use of the word 'Easter' by the translators in **Acts 12:1-5**;

*Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.) And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people. Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.*

The argument states that since the translators had chosen to use the neologism of William Tyndall, 'Passover' in all other instances where the term 'Pascha' appears in scripture, that either the translation is an error, or they were signifying a completely different feast than Passover. 

The transliterated word pascha, from Ancient Greek πάσχα (páskha), from Aramaic פַּסְחָא (paskha), from Hebrew פֶּסַח (pésakh), was used throughout scripture to refer to the Passover feast of the Lord and the feast of Unleavened Bread that follows, commemorating the use of the blood of the lamb, signifying Christ, and the Exodus from Egypt, signifying salvation by the mighty hand of God. 

Obviously, those claiming it is a translation error are wrong. The KJV is the inspired and preserved word of God in English. Without error. 

But those who should know better claim that the translators made this choice to change what term they used to translate Pascha to teach a secret doctrine of a feast to Astare/Asteroth that Herod was keeping, separate from the Jewish feast. 

This is nonsense. 

The primary argument is that "Passover is a day. Not the entire week long feast of Unleavened Bread, and it says after Easter, so it can't refer to Passover day! Thus it is a pagan holiday."

This is begging the question. The premises are not true, and so the assumption made isn't an argument. 

**Luke 22:1***
Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.*

Same author as Acts, Luke. Same word being translated, here as Passover, in **Acts 12**, Easter. The Bible defining itself, it refers to the entire feast. All the days. 

See also **Deuteronomy 16:1-3**, which refers to Passover and Unleavened Bread as one, long feast;

*Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God: for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night.Thou shalt therefore sacrifice the passover unto the Lord thy God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which the Lord shall choose to place his name there. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction; for thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste: that thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life.*

So we know that these were the *days* of unleavened bread, that Herod sought to please the Jews, and so he arrested Peter, intending to bring him forth to the people, to be executed like James had been, after Pascha had ended. After the feast of Unleavened Bread. After Passover. After Easter. 

There is no other argument made in this regard that comes from scripture. And there is no argument put forth using scripture that supports the claim that this refers to a pagan feast, rather than the Pascha of the Lord. 

That the translators used the only chronological mention of Passover, the feast of Unleavened Bread, that appears in scripture, following the resurrection, to refer to the feast using the English term Christians called it, differentiating the OT understanding from the NT, is in my opinion a deliberate choice. Again, the Bible defining itself.

And the final nail in the coffin of this weird doctrine, that the translators were not talking about the Passover feast, from the feast of the Lord through resurrection Sunday, which takes place during the days of Unleavened Bread, but were actually cluing us in to Herod being a pagan celebrating a feast to Asteroth, is that they included this handy chart to track the days given the difference between the Gregorian calendar and the shifting lunar calendar used by the Hebrews to mark the days. 

"To find Easter for ever." They were not including a means to find the date of a pagan festival. They knew what the word meant to Christians for hundreds of years before them. Easter being used by the earlier translators in place of Pascha, who didn't rely on Tyndall's newly invented 'Passover.' 

It is preposterous to claim to be KJVO and then say the translators included a pagan holiday calendar in it. 

They did not make an error and they did not mean a feast for Astare.

They meant the Pascha, and the risen Christ.

"But there are pagan spring holidays that have rabbits and eggs and fertility ceremonies and sacrifices! Modern use of a bunny and baskets with chocolate eggs are pagan, so the entire thing must be rejected!" 

Again, pagans do a lot of things that they copied from God. The first animal sacrifice is God teaching Adam and Eve about Jesus. Pagans do animal sacrifices too. I guess God was teaching them to be pagans. 

Just because localized cultural traditions spring up (no pun intended) around Christian holy days, doesn't make the holy day wrong. 

When a pastor or someone claiming to be a teacher brings forth a strange doctrine that cannot be proven from scripture, but relies on a fallacious argument, extra biblical sources and teaching for commandments the doctrines of men, judging those who disagree or trying to sow doubtful disputations with those weak in the faith, search the scriptures to see if it is so. The Bible is the final authority.

**Colossians 2:16-17**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.*

One more thing; invariably, almost without fail, the people who push these internet doctrines the hardest, that seek to make celebration of Christ's birth, death and resurrection into pagan festivals to discourage Christians from celebrating, are hardcore Judaizers. 

Lots of sincere Bible-believing, soul winning, separated Christians get caught up in these things, and are just trying to do the right thing for the Lord, as their conscience sees it. **This is not about them**. I want to make that very very clear. 

But the ones who seem to push the notion that "Celebrating traditional Christian holidays is actually pagan. So don't do it!" the most are Hebrew roots types. Like the one who just spammed my chat with some nonsense meme using "hashem" and other Jewish terms to say if you celebrate Easter you aren't saved. 

Jews main argument against Christianity is that it is a pagan religion. They push their noahide law doctrines on Gentiles, that flat out states worshiping of Christ is Idolatry, punishable by death. By beheading. 

And to that end, they promote things like the pagan origins of holy days, and push Christians to adopt Hebrew feasts. To keep the Sabbath. To blow the shofar. 

It is no wonder that churches heavily influenced by dispensationalism, Zionism, and the pre-tribulation rapture, also often fall prey to these memes. They will also teach things like the Satan seed heresy, that nephilim are half breeds, and that "God is not done with Israel yet."

I think dispensationalism is a foot in the door for Judaizers. And Jewish fables claiming that Christianity is just Mithraism, that Enoch is hidden scripture, or that Easter is a pagan holiday, are deliberately done to make the name of Christ be hid. To bring us under bondage. As a snare.

That false churches like the Roman Catholics do pagan things in their religion gives these Judaizers ammunition. They feed each other and do the work of Satan.

teachings.title: The red heifer and the burnt offerings pictured Christ
teachings.summary: Reads the red heifer of Numbers 19 and the Levitical sacrifices as pictures of Christ already fulfilled, warning against the idea that they are a prophecy for the Jews today.
teachings.text:
The burnt offerings in the Old Testament were all a picture of Christ Jesus. Not a prophecy of the Jews today. See **👇**

**Numbers 19**
*And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

2 This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke:

3 And ye shall give her unto Eleazar the priest, that he may bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:

4 And Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood directly before the tabernacle of the congregation seven times:

5 And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:

6 And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

7 Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the even.

8 And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the even.

9 And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water of separation: it is a purification for sin.

*
The foolish and unbiblical "Red Heifer prophecy" was created in 1989 by an American Pentecostal preacher who practiced Zionist-dispensationalism, and who decided that, since he bred red cattle, and one of the carnal ordinances included a burnt offering of a red heifer, that should the Jews offer one, they could usher in the end times, forcing God's judgment and the second coming of Christ. 

Since then, Jews have been using this half-assed prophecy to fundraise off of gullible Christians misled by Scofield, wicked TV charismatics funded by Israel, and a generation of pastors trained to teach the worship of Jews over Christ. 

We see clearly in the one mention of a red heifer, that it was yet another picture of Christ Jesus. The cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet, present during the time Abraham set to offer his son Issac, upon the same hill Jesus would later be crucified on, and included in many of the burnt offerings described in the Levitical laws, all of which pictured Christ. 

The cedar of the cross. The hyssop soaked in vinegar. The scarlet of His blood given for us. The oblation given of a spotless sacrifice. A propitiation for our sin. To whom no yoke had ever been upon. 

This false teaching is having renewed interest today, as the Jews who say they are but are not, but do lie, attempt to join in the propaganda campaign going on now to meme judgment day into being. To trick God, and despair men. 

Don't be fooled! God's timing is His own and the sacrifices of the Old Testament were a picture of His Son, who has come already and in whom the sins of the world have already been paid by the blood He shed. He was the burnt offering, in Hell three days and nights, and resurrected into glory, overcoming the world. With the keys to Hell and Death. 

Be at peace in Jesus. Let no man deceive you. Be not afraid.

Remember that this is the reason God destroyed Israel and brought judgement upon Judah. Child sacrifice, as the Canaanites did.

teachings.title: What 'led captivity captive' means
teachings.summary: Shows from Judges 5 that leading captivity captive means taking one's captors captive, and applies it to Christ rising from three days in Hell with victory over death and Hell, not freeing captives from Hell.
teachings.text:
**Judges 5:12-13**
*Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam. Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the Lord made me have dominion over the mighty.*

**Psalm 68:12-19**
*Kings of armies did flee apace: and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though ye have lien among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold. When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.

The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; an high hill as the hill of Bashan. Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever. The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place. 

Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the Lord God might dwell among them. Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.*

**Ephesians 4:4-10**
*There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men. (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth? He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)*

**Hebrews 2:14**
*Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;*

In case anyone was wondering what "led captivity captive" means, here is the Biblical concept, first defined in Judges 5, as Deborah and Barak sing a victory prayer after they had defeated Israel's oppressors and made those kings and their nations who had enslaved them their slaves. 

In a like manner, Jesus who was captive in Hell for 3 days and 3 nights, rose from the dead, bodily, led captivity captive, as He had victory and took power over death and Hell.

Misunderstanding what that phrase means has led many to believe false teachers who claim it means Jesus freed captives in Hell.

No. He freed mankind from the bonds of death and Hell. He took captive His captors.

teachings.title: Passover and the timing of the crucifixion
teachings.summary: Lines up the Passover week with Christ's triumphal entry, betrayal, crucifixion and resurrection, and argues that letting the Bible set the timing gives three days and three nights rather than the Good Friday tradition.
teachings.text:
I'm not 100% positive, but if today is Passover then we are aligned with the same schedule of events as the Passover of Jesus' crucifixion. 

Saturday, His triumphant entry into Jerusalem, the 10th day of their month, Adar. Tuesday night, the last supper and betrayal by Judas and arrest in the garden of Gethsemane. Today, brought before the High Priests, the lamb without blemish. Slain before the assembled people. Taken down from the cross and buried by 6PM tonight. Eventime. Three days and nights in Hell, three Sabbaths in a row, Passover, the first day of unleavened bread, Saturday. Risen on the first day of the week, Sunday. 

Because our calendar isn't the same as the ancient Hebrews, and the lunar calendar and because they reckon days 6PM to 6PM, not at midnight as we do, it doesn't line up precisely each year.  

One interesting note is that in the Talmud, according to the wicked Maimonides, Jews may never celebrate a passover on a Wednesday. (The timing given in the OT by God through Moses sets a specific date, regardless of timing).

Modern Jews use the Catholic tradition of claiming the Last Supper was a passover seder on Maundy Thursday to throw doubt on the Gospels. That, and the Good Friday narrative make it that the supper wasn't on Passover, and that Jesus would have only been dead one full day, Saturday, and possibly 2 nights under that formula, gives Jews ammunition to argue Jesus didn't fulfill the scriptures. That it was not 3 days and 3 nights, using the Catholic doctrine. 

But of course it's their doctrine that's wrong, and when we allow the Bible to set the timing, we get to see just how the original passover and God's ordinance regarding it, and the other spring feasts, tie directly to Jesus. The foreshadowing of Christ. It is beautiful and perfect.

Another foolish argument comes from people who insist the modern calendar dates 33AD as having Jesus die on a Friday. Of course they are placing a man made calendar over the preserved and inspired word of God.

teachings.title: The Scarlet Thread
teachings.summary: Traces the scarlet thread from the hand of Zarah in Genesis 38 through Rahab in Joshua 2 and the genealogy of Matthew 1 as a picture of the blood of Christ.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 38:28**
 
*And it came to pass, when she travailed, that the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.*



**Joshua 2:18**
 
*Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee.*

"The Bible also mentions scarlet thread or scarlet yarn as part of the tabernacle’s curtains (Exodus 26:1) and the high priest’s ephod (Exodus 28:6), along with threads of gold, blue, and purple. Scripture does not comment on the significance of those colors in the curtains or ephod, but some commentators surmise that the gold, blue, and purple foreshadow Christ’s glory, heavenly origin, and kingly position, while the scarlet thread represents Christ’s atoning work on the cross through the shedding of His blood."

**Matthew 1** genealogy from Abraham to Joseph, husband of Mary shows the scarlet thread running through the Bible from these instances. And* Judas begat **Phares** and Zara of Thamar; and **Phares** begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram..And Salmon begat Booz of **Rachab**; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse.*..on to Jesus.

teachings.title: The blood of the covenant and thanksgiving
teachings.summary: The Old Covenant sacrifices sealed in blood pictured Christ's once-for-all sacrifice, and God never needed them but desires thanksgiving, mercy and right judgment.
teachings.text:
The covenant was made by sacrifice; the blood of the covenant made by Moses and the people with God was sealed with blood that represented the blood of Christ, and the promise of a better covenant with God by sacrifice, the sacrifice of the Son.

**Hebrews 9:19–23**
*For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.*

The heavens declare the righteousness of Christ Jesus, and His righteousness is upon all His people. God is the judge Himself. The Atonement, Himself. The mediator, Himself.

The saints are secure in His righteousness. But God speaks to Israel in judgment. Beginning with His people.

*Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.*

The future prophecy versus the current call.

The continuous sacrifices made before God to give the physical nation of Israel the honor of being His people, keep His hand from reproving them harshly. They maintained the Levitical ordinances which He based promises on. The sacrifices that needed to be done constantly to maintain ritual cleanliness and keep His presence among them had been done. He isn't asking for more sacrifice. No additional bulls or goats to shed their blood.

Again, we have a better sacrifice, once and for all, a covenant made by the blood of Jesus, the burnt offering for our sin.

**Hebrews 9:11–14**
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?*

But, in the old covenant, the blood of bulls and goats were used, continually, signifying the Sacrifice to come, and this the Levites did.

God is telling His people at this time He isn't asking for more, and in fact it is not the blood of bulls and goats, and their burnt offering that He seeks.

Every beast is His. The cattle upon a thousand hills. If He were hungry, and in need of the savour of the fat and the sustenance of meats, He has His pick and fill. He doesn't need them. Their sacrifices are a picture and a necessity for the covenant, but they do not please Him in and of themselves.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

Sentiment repeated by Christ;

**Matthew 12:7**
*But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.*

Here, in **Psalm 50**, God makes it clear that the offering is thanksgiving. They are vows to be paid to maintain their part in the covenant as His nation. Tithes and first fruits as acts of faith.

It is not, as other gods, a meal for Him to consume, but a thanksgiving offered to show gratitude for all that He has supplied them, and to keep themselves unspotted, and be His people.

God desires mercy towards others. Right judgment, defending the weak and hating the workers of iniquity.

teachings.title: Dark sayings made plain in Christ
teachings.summary: Parables and dark sayings filter the humble from the spiritually blind, but Christ opened all the Old Testament to show it points to Him, and the Spirit now reveals its meaning to believers.
teachings.text:
The call by David to hear and understand his "dark sayings and parables," brings to mind the way Jesus taught in His ministry.

**Matthew 13:34–35**
*All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world*.

Jesus revealed to His disciples that parables act as a spiritual filter. To the humble seeker of wisdom, they provide deeper understanding; to the spiritually blind, they remain obscure "dark sayings."

**Matthew 13:10–13**
*And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables? He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand*.

The unfolding revelation to man throughout scripture was never meant to keep wisdom hidden. Especially, not forever.

Unlike the religions of man, with their esoteric knowledge, vague and shallow sayings fed in dribs and drabs, with no clarity ever given, God's word opens itself up, and Jesus ultimately shows what all these "dark sayings" and prophetic parables actually mean.

 **John 16:25**
*These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.*

During His earthly ministry, even Jesus' most faithful disciples required His explanation of the parables He spoke in, to the crowds and Pharisees.

**Mark 4:33–34**
*And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.*

But the full revelation of scripture came in the days following His resurrection, when all things were finally made known.

To the men He met on the way, in **Luke 24**, Jesus, *beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself*.

And to the gathering of the disciples, He did the same;

**Luke 24:44–45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*.

He explicitly references the three divisions of the Old Testament, (the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms, like Psalm 49) and grants them the spiritually supernatural ability to finally see past the "dark sayings" to understand the plain truth of the Gospel.

These things are revealed to us by the Spirit, Who teaches us all things. We are able to see the entire picture, fully revealed in Christ, and the understanding imparted by the Apostles in the Epistles for added clarity and depth. Only the future Revelation of Christ Jesus is still through a glass darkly, (although the gist is pretty clear on timing and events).

We see that the Old Testament scriptures aren't an empty recitation of genealogy, geography and events. They aren't the vain contemplations of man. They are the words of eternal life, and all these were written to point the way to Jesus, and provide us with understanding.

**1 Corinthians 10:11**
*Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

Not only does God's word exist to show us His ways, but ultimately it is the tool He has given us to fulfill the Great Commission, leading others to the truth.

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: Christ the King of all the earth
teachings.summary: Psalm 47 prophesies Jesus, who is God, ascending with a shout and returning with a trumpet to catch up the saints, reign as King of kings over every nation, and finally deliver the kingdom to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 47** is a song of praise for the Lord, the King of kings. Christ Jesus, Who shall put every nation under His feet.

**Revelation 11:15–17**
*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O LORD God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

He shall rule and reign with a rod of iron, and give to all His people their inheritance in His Kingdom.

Jesus is God. Verse 5 says *God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.* A prophetic Old Testament verse, made clear in the New Testament, carrying the comfort of all believers;

**1 Thessalonians 4:16–17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

We shall sing of the glories of the Lord, forever.

**Revelation 7:10–12**
*And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.*

**Revelation 19:16**
*And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.*

For Jesus is the King of all the earth, and reigns over the heathen. All the nations. He is greatly exalted above every name.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus will reign over all things, and, having defeated death and been made ruler of all, He will give all to God the Father. A perfect sacrifice, holy and acceptable, made holy by His righteousness:

**1 Corinthians 15:24–27**
*Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him*.

**Psalm 47** is a wonderful and prophetic song of praise and worship for the Kingdom of God, under our Lord Christ Jesus. All honor and praise is His. Amen

teachings.title: Their drink offerings of blood: the Mass refuted
teachings.summary: Roman Catholic drink offerings and repeated sacrifice of the Mass are offerings to another god, while Christ's blood was offered once for all.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 16**, David calls out the vanity and ultimate end of those that call not upon the Lord for salvation. Who go after another god.

They make drink offerings of blood, and speak other names in their prayers.

The most prominent example of this today is Roman Catholicism. They make drink offerings, claiming it to be the blood of Christ, profaning His name, and bow to and serve idols representing their own gods.

But for the saved, the Lord is our inheritance, we are co-heirs with Christ the Bible says, and He is our cup, the blood shed for us on the cross:

**Luke 22:20**
*Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.*

The very new testament which we preach is founded upon the blood shed by Jesus. Not a chalice of gold held up by a priest to an image, sacrificing Jesus daily, as if that were possible or necessary, to call Him down from heaven again.

And it is God that maintains our lot. Who holds us by His power. Not carnal sacrifices made over and over again.

**Hebrews 10:10–14**
*By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.*

This is our goodly heritage. This is the promise of God. The Son at the right hand of the Father. We shall not be moved. And so we rejoice.

We rest in hope.

teachings.title: Jesus is the excellent name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Psalm 8 praises Christ, who is God, the Creator through whom all things were made, the I AM given the name above every name, and the only name under heaven by which men must be saved and worshipped.
teachings.text:
The excellent name of our Lord is Jesus.

**Psalm 8** is a song of praise for the Christ. The name of the Lord, who has been set by the LORD, God the Father, over all things. Who also is God.

Jesus is the anointed, Who is ordained to strength, and mighty.

**Hebrews 2:4–9**
*God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.*

The New Testament reveals the intent and interpretation of the Old. We see Jesus using Psalm 8:2 against the Pharisees, showing that He is the name of God;

**Matthew 21:15–17**
*And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased, And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise? And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there*.

Through His name was all creation made:

**Colossians 1:16–17**
*For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

**John 1:1–3**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.*

*The same was in the beginning*, when men first called upon the name of the Lord.

**Genesis 4:25–26**
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

Jesus has been made to have dominion over all things, that the glory and honor be given to Him.

**Ephesians 1:9–10**
*Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him*

And the excellency of His name is revealed in Christ Jesus.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus is the name of the Lord. Of the great I Am.

**John 8:56–58**
*Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.*

No other name is given by God to be worshipped as God.

**Acts 4:12**
*Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.*

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: Whom the Lord loveth he correcteth
teachings.summary: God's chastening when we stray is a mark that we are sons and should be received with thanks, and Wisdom, by which God founded the earth, is Jesus Himself, the way and the tree of life.
teachings.text:
*My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.*

Gaining wisdom and understanding comes also from His chastening when we don't keep to His paths, when we stray to our own understanding. Like a mule that may wander off the path is whipped, so too are we chastened. And we should be thankful.

**Hebrews 12:7-8** *ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

Be happy in chastening. Delight in His law. Gain understanding, covet Wisdom the way men covet riches, because it is more precious than silver, gold or rubies or any of the merchandise of the world.

Wealth cannot extend your life and give you health, not like the Lord can. And love of money is the root of all evil, and for covetousness sake come wars. But pursuing Wisdom brings life.

*Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour.*

Her paths lead to peace. Wisdom is a tree of life! So by faith we step out on the paths, and keep the commandments, understanding the promises of God.

The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth. Creation is by His knowledge and understanding. And knowing all things were created by His Word, through Christ Jesus, we see that Jesus IS the way, the truth, the light that is described throughout Proverbs. He is Wisdom. He is the tree of life. We are followers of the Way. We follow Jesus.

teachings.title: Job restored when he prayed for his friends
teachings.summary: Job made peace with God by faith, but it was his forgiving and praying for the friends who wronged him, a picture of Christ the mediator, that led God to restore him double.
teachings.text:
Job, having seen the glory of God, His power and might, he says he has uttered what he understood not. In ignorance, he demanded of God the "why" to his predicament, and now sees the Who behind all things. He has gained understanding and repented towards the truth of the power of God. Left humbled in the dust and ash of his mourning.

This settled, Job has gained the the understanding that God does what He does, at a higher purpose and longer view than His creation can even comprehend.

The Lord then turns to Eliphaz and the two friends, saying they kindled His wrath, having spoken falsely about Him. Things that aren't right. Their prosperity gospel theology and their standing in judgment as if they were God Himself against Job was wrong.

And He tells them to make sacrifices and offer burnt offerings, and Job's prayers for forgiveness for them He will accept. This act of humiliation, seeking forgiveness through the man they had slandered, is done according to God's word, and the Lord accepted Job.

This, in a way is symbolic of Christ as the mediator between God and man, as Job is the mediator here for his friends.

And when Job prayed for his friends, the Lord turned the captivity of Job, the allowances of the devil to control his fate, and restored Job twice as much as he had.

In all these things Job never spoke improperly, but in ignorance demanded of God. But it was Job's forgiveness of others who had wronged him that led God to restore him, and bless him with more than he had.

Job reached peace with God just by his understanding and faith. But it was forgiveness of others that restored him. This is such an important point to remember.

Job first receives the comforting and support, from family and friends, that he needed. And their financial support to him that was without, allowed Job to restore his wealth. The love and respect Job had shown others paid off, as they loved on him with emotional support and alms. Gold and riches he used to make his flocks great again.

And God blessed him with 10 children, seven sons and 3 daughters. And Jobs delight in his daughters, naming them for peace, and fragrant spice and beauty, led him to make them co-heirs as their brothers.

teachings.title: I know that my redeemer liveth
teachings.summary: Job confesses his living Redeemer, Christ, who will stand on the earth, and his hope to see God in his flesh in the resurrection.
teachings.text:
After the merciless railing by Bildad, Job again offers his defense. He lists in all the ways that God has clearly set against him, and the reproach he has become to those around him. His friends, family, kin, wife. All are opposed to him in his sorry state.

Job is destroyed on every side.

He wonders how much more these three friends will continue to break him further with words. He is indignant at their attitudes, that they feel no shame in beating a man when he's down.

He says, if they want to continue to pile on him, know that God has done this and more, and they aren't God. He begs his friends, "Have pity upon me, for the hand of God hath touched me."

This is all he asked for from them. Not belaboring the obvious and accusing him relentlessly, rubbing his nose in his plight.

And then Job makes a general plea to the Heavens, with a profession that is clear:

*Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever! For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth*

We know his words were preserved, forever by the power of God, and his confession of Faith in his living redeemer, his Savior, Who shall stand in the latter day upon the earth. Christ Jesus.

Job says, even after his corrupt flesh is destroyed, his mortal body gone, that in his flesh he shall see God. The resurrection is his hope and he knows he will see it come. His own eyes will witness the Lord in that day. The same blessed hope we share to this day.

And this truth Job holds in his heart, despite all the suffering he has experienced, makes him fear for his erstwhile friends.

If he suffered, be afraid. For the wrath of God is obviously real. And fear it. That rather than their cruelty, they should ask themselves why they do it, given God has done enough. They should fear the same recompense for their behavior, and repent.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple points to Christ the true temple
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple was the high pattern for a repentant nation to restore God's glory, and Israel's falling short points to Christ who is the true temple.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Ezekiel's Temple continues, and with much of the measurements and ordinances given, the prophet, and the angelic man with him, witness the return of the glory of God through the east gate, as Ezekiel says, in the like manner he had watched Him depart in the vision of destruction seen in **Ezekiel 9-11**.

*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern*.

Here, we are given the purpose of this vision. That this is the pattern of what an ashamed and chastened people would need to restore the glory of God in their midst.

The Lord provides the details of the altar and the sacrifices. The priests and the atonement. The sins of the people are great, putting up pillars to their gods where His temple was, His footstool. The corpses of their kings placed where the sanctified and holy unto God were meant to be. Abominations that caused the desolation and destruction. Restitution and reconciliation offered by ritual cleansing and a resumption of the sacrifices and sin offering.

Another theory regarding Ezekiel's temple is that it is a picture of the Temple in Eternity. That when the last of creation is burned like a scroll, and a New Heaven and New Earth have been given us by God, that this temple would be in place.

Of course, only those justified in Christ Jesus will remain, and our sins will He remember no more.

Our sanctification and redemption will be long past, washed clean in Christ.

So we reject this theory as well.

Given the context of **Ezekiel 43**, we can understand that this is the model of what God would require for a repentant Jewish people, to fully restore the glory among them. The model given them as a nation. Not individual salvation, which is always personal, and by faith in the promises of God, but as a people. A nation. Blessed to have the Lord among them.

The standards were high. Near impossible. But achievable, or God wouldn't have presented it to them. But like the Law, all have fallen short.

**Haggai 2:3**
*Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?*

The temple would never return to this Glory, until the temple of Christ came, was torn down, and on the third day raised up.

**John 2:19-20**
*Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body.*

**Ezekiel 43**’s vision of a glorious temple, when compared to the historical reality of the 2nd Temple, suggests a “falling short” that points to a greater fulfillment. Taken in that point of view, it underscores the need for Jesus Christ, who embodies the true temple, restores God’s presence, and fulfills the prophetic hope of a renewed covenant. And with it a new nation, of every kindred and tongue. The Kingdom of God.

teachings.title: Only the blood atones
teachings.summary: Says turning over a new leaf, baptism, joining a church or good deeds cannot satisfy the price of sin, and that only Christ's blood offered on the mercy seat propitiates, with Hebrews 9 quoted.
teachings.text:
Turning your life around, repenting of sin, joining a church, getting water baptized, making Jesus the Lord of your life, seeing real change, sacraments and good deeds... None of these things satisfy the price of sin. 

Only the blood of a holy God offered in our place and sprinkled on the mercy seat can atone for our sin and justify us before God. That is the only propitiation. The blood is for the heavenly Father.

**Hebrews 9:11-26** 
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, **but by his own blood** he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.

It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others; For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.*

**Romans 3:25**
*Whom God hath set forth to be a **propitiation** **through faith in his blood**, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God*

teachings.title: Come, buy without money and without price
teachings.summary: Isaiah 55 echoes Jesus' call to come and drink freely, salvation by grace at no cost, and the word as seed that will not return void.
teachings.text:
Again, Isaiah is given the prophecy of Christ Jesus and the coming of the Holy One of Israel.

The chapter opens with a call to come and drink freely, to eat without money, without a price. Just as Jesus preaches throughout the gospels, especially **John 6** **and 7**.

**John 6:35**
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.*

**John 7:37**
*If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.*

By grace, at no cost to us. Not the bread that satisfies not, paid for by our labors. But being full of His word, the goodness we delight in.

*Hear, and your soul shall live and I will make an everlasting covenant with you.* You can hear the voice of Jesus echoing to Isaiah.

A light to lighten the Gentiles, the nations that knew not.

*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near.*

The Lord has mercy on those who turns unto Him, for God will abundantly pardon our sins.

His word is the precious seed we bear as we share the gospel. And it will not return void. It will bring forth fruit, being seed to the sower and bread to the eater.

The picture of salvation by growing grain, just as Jesus preaches by parable. To the Lord, the increase. The harvest.

And we shall come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves. Amen

teachings.title: The tabernacle of David raised up
teachings.summary: Unbelieving Israel was disowned like the heathen, while the fallen tabernacle of David is raised in Christ for the remnant of Gentiles called by His name.
teachings.text:
The word of the Lord, as preached by Amos, contains very clear language and promises. Not as rich in dark saying and vague symbols as people portray the books of the prophets.

He tells Amos, smite the lintel of the door that the posts shake and fall on the heads of the Israelites, and the Lord will slay all of them with the sword. A reverse Passover, where the blood of the lamb on the lintel saved the people.

No matter where they seek to hide, the Lord shall have their lives. Dug underground to Hell, the tops of mountains, the bottom of the sea, even surrendering to captivity, there is no escaping the wrath against Israel, nor the end times wrath it pictures.

The Lord is mighty, and all powerful. Amen! The Lord is His name.

*Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the Lord. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?*

The Israelites of the Northern Kingdom are utterly disowned. No better than the Ethiopian. Just as He took the children of Israel from Egypt, He says, so too He took the Philistines from Caphtor, which is Crete and the Syrians from Southern Babylon, which is Kir. They aren't the only nation taken and moved by God to a new land, and made mighty. And they aren't the only people He chooses to destroy.

It is humbling to know He thinks no more of these people, called by His name and who betrayed Him, than the heathen nations who are their enemies.

*Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.*

Because that remnant of Jacob will lead to Christ, and the promise the Lord made unto David, and the place, Jerusalem, which He placed His name, in Jesus.

He sifted them as He does all nations. And all the sinners of His people slain. Wew.

With the promise of wrath and destruction, God the long-suffering and merciful offers that blessed hope.

*In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.*

Jesus, the Son of David, restored to His throne in His Kingdom. And the promise is not just to believing Israel, or to the "Jews," but even to Edom, to the heathen which are called by His name. To the remnant of the Gentiles that believe on Christ. His people, Israel, to the paradise of His eternal Kingdom.

A*nd they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God*.

teachings.title: Spared for David's sake and Jerusalem's
teachings.summary: Judah was spared only for God's promise to David and for Jerusalem, pointing to Christ, not for the sake of the Jews.
teachings.text:
Amos preaches against Jerusalem, Zion, where they feel safe in their sins compared to the North. Their wealth and palaces hated by God.

The Lord describes their land as better than any in all Assyria, or of the Philistines. Their riches and excess in food. Their luxury of being able to work on music and new instruments, comfortable beds, drinking wine out of bowls. He promised their destruction.

Tearing down the great houses. Killing the princess there. Captivity and affliction. They aren't going to escape His judgement.

It is important to keep in mind that God only kept Judah from being utterly destroyed like the rest of Israel, for two reasons; His promise to David that Jesus would come from his line, and the city Jerusalem, where He chose to place His name.

People who place the importance of Jerusalem on the Jews who occupy it, that Judah was spared destruction for their sakes', somehow, aren't rightly dividing the word. It is plain and clear:

**1 Kings 11:32**
*But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel*.

This explanation is given by God repeatedly, leading up to the judgment against Israel and the Babylonian captivity, and it only makes sense in the context of Christ Jesus.

**Isaiah 1:9**
*Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah*.

That remnant includes the 14 generations from David to Jesus.

teachings.title: Crying unto the Lord from the depths
teachings.summary: Jonah's prayer, like David's Psalms, shows the believer in distress turning to the Lord with thanksgiving, knowing He hears and delivers even from the depths.
teachings.text:
**Jonah 2** in light of the Gospels, shows the reluctant prophet as a type of Jesus, the willing Son. The three days and nights in Hell being the sign Jesus said would be ignored by the Jews, even as the Gentiles of Nineveh received the word.

The prayer of Jonah echos many lines of the Psalms, where David cries out for salvation, calling upon the name of the Lord for relief.

**Psalm 69:1-3**
*Save me, O God; For the waters are come in unto my soul. I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me. I am weary of my crying: my throat is dried: Mine eyes fail while I wait for my God.*

The form and function of the prayer, like the Psalms, show us how we should be in times of distress and tribulation. Constantly turning to the Lord to be our salvation, remembering His loving kindness. Thanksgiving in the face of adversity. Knowing God will not forsake you or fail you.

When we are at the end of our rope, our soul fainting, we can know He hears us. Even at the depths of the sea. Even were we in Hell itself. The Lord hears and delivers us. Amen.

teachings.title: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice
teachings.summary: The sacrifices only pictured Christ, the one true offering, and God's will is that we know Him and show others the mercy He showed us, unlike goodness that fades like the morning dew.
teachings.text:
Hosea continues prophesying against Israel, primarily Ephraim and here, Gilead which is a territory of Manasseh, East of the Jordan, but also the Southern Kingdom of Judah. There are false gods, idols, and worse, violence and murder among them.

The prophet begins with an appeal to repentance, turning towards the Lord to heal that which He has smitten them with in His righteous wrath. He says if they do, on the 3rd day they would be risen up, a prophetic reference to the resurrection of Christ.

He says, *Then shall we know, if we follow in to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared as the morning*; Christ's coming was preordained and as inevitable as the sunrise, the morning star.
