His coming as the rain, the former rains of the spring, the later rains of fall and the harvest. I believe that is prophetic of the two comings of Jesus. Just as the Spring and Fall feasts point to His first and second coming. These rains bringing life in abundance.

He follows this comparison of Jesus to the seasonal rains with a lament if the goodness of Israel, which Hosea compares to the fleeting morning cloud, or the quick to evaporate dew upon the grass.

In relation to the Christian life, I have experienced this of myself. The intents of the morning to pick up that cross, beginning the day with prayer and scripture, only to see the goodness fade with the day like the dew. Drawing the stray moisture from the air around us, rather than being soaked in the rains, and so losing steam throughout the day.

The Lord has slain them with His word, reproved by the prophets speaking in the Spirit, the law convicting them for their deeds. His judgments as a light, piercing the darkness of their sin.

*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

**Psalm 40:6-8**
*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart*.

**Hebrews 10:7-10**
*Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all*.

God's will for us is that we show the same mercy towards others He extended to us. The sacrifices and ordinances of the OT were for their understanding, that the children of God had a means of picturing the sacrifice of Christ to come, Jesus being the only true sacrifice for sin. But the blood of the testament with God for forgiveness and eternal life exists as a gift for our benefit, that we may know we have that relationship. That we become sons of God, so that we may know love. Mercy. Charity. His will for our lives and our obedience, that it be well with us. Jesus is the door. But there is a pasture He leads us to, in rest that we can magnify His light to guide others from the darkness.

teachings.title: Bidding all to the Passover feast
teachings.summary: Hezekiah's call to all Israel to the Passover, a picture of Christ, is like the king's wedding parable where many made excuses but bad and good were compelled to come and were pardoned.
teachings.text:
The revival led by King Hezekiah continues, and he leads the great restoration of the Passover, the feast of unleavened bread, which is given to Israel as a picture of Christ.

The King bidding all Israel to the feast of the lamb slain for their iniquity is similar to this parable told by Jesus in **Matthew 22:1-10**

*And Jesus answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said, The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son, And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come. Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage. But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them. But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city. Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy. Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage. So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.*

Just as with Hezekiah's letters to all Israel, many made excuses, or mocked the invitation. But many were compelled to come, turning their heart to the Lord.

And as Jesus' parable, both bad and good came. People who were ceremonially unclean, yet sought after the Lord God of Israel. And Hezekiah begs their pardon of the Lord, and our merciful God grants it, a picture of the fact that while we were yet sinners Christ died for us.

teachings.title: The remnant of Israel and the daughter of Zion
teachings.summary: Zephaniah's promise to the remnant applies beyond the return from Babylon to Christ's followers and all believers in New Jerusalem, whom the false Jews of the synagogue of Satan will come to worship before.
teachings.text:
And so the prophecy given Zephaniah turns to the rebuke facing the holy city in that time. God says he will remove from there the haughty and prideful, the corrupt leaders and wicked men of Jerusalem, killed or carried away into captivity.

But, as we saw in **2 Kings**, and in **Jeremiah**, God left behind a remnant, of the poor and the afflicted. Left by Babylon to be laborers in the field. To work the vineyard. To tend to the flocks and be husbandmen to the land. And they shall trust in the name of the Lord.

*The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.*

This prophetic verse refers primarily to those left behind from the captivity, but is also talking about the believers who followed Christ in His ministry, the Apostles and disciples, and applies to the larger Christian population through the ages, and especially to those of us saved, in the resurrection, in New Jerusalem. What a wonderful picture of that glorious day.

*Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.*

These final verses are more than just the promise to return the captives from Babylon, 70 years later. It is an eternal promise to we, as believers.

Our King in the midst of us, seeing evil no more. Our transgressions gone. No fear. Working the vineyards of the Lord, His servants forevermore. He will save us, and rejoice over us. Singing songs of joy, resting in love. And

*I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden.*

**Luke 4:14-19**
*And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

And the promise to make us a name among all the people of the earth, to let the unbelieving know that He has loved us, and that we are not ashamed, reminds me of Jesus prophecy in **Revelation 3:9**;

*Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.*

What a wonderful God, Who loves us so!

teachings.title: Hezekiah broke the brazen serpent Nehushtan
teachings.summary: The brazen serpent was a picture of Christ lifted up, but Hezekiah rightly destroyed it when it was worshipped, refuting Catholics who use it to justify images.
teachings.text:
Here in chapter 18, we begin to learn of King Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, king of Judah. *And he* *did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father did.*

He not only did that which was right, but broke down the high places and the images, and cut down the groves where the heathen worshiped. He even destroyed the brazen serpent, called Nehishtan, which Moses had made when the firey serpents were killing the children of Israel in their camp in the wilderness.

**Numbers 21:8-9**
*And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.*

This was, of course, a picture of Christ.

**John 3:14-15**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.*

While Nehishtan's original purpose was to serve as a picture of Christ, showing that the children of Israel looked to it and lived, just as we look to Christ lifted up on the cross and have eternal life, the brazen serpent was never itself meant to be an object of worship. Men weren't to bow and serve it. It had a specific purpose, and that purpose was past.

Catholics and their schismatics in other denominations, use the brazen serpent to justify their idolatry. They say that if God told Moses to make this particular image, then the making of any image is allowed. And they proceed to bow and serve them, lighting candles and incense to them, and pray at their feet.

They seldom have ever heard of Nehishtan. They don't know the story of Hezekiah. They don't know he destroyed it because the children of Israel were treating it the way Catholics treat images of the crucifix, of Mary and various other humans.

That the word of God says Hezekiah did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord and destroyed it. They err not knowing scripture, determined to keep their groves and high places and their images they make. To worship outside of the ways God had given in His word. Keeping to vain traditions and dead works.

teachings.title: The plague stayed at Araunah's threshing floor
teachings.summary: The plague stayed at Jerusalem pictures God shortening the great tribulation for the elect's sake before the rapture and wrath, and David paying for the altar pictures Christ paying for our sins.
teachings.text:
The final chapter of **2 Samuel** tells a tale from some point in King David's reign, where God is angry with the people of Israel, and in His anger he allows Satan to tempt David into sin that they may be punished. And so David comes to desire a census of the people, ordering Joab and his captains to number the people.

David as king wants to know the number of men for his own purpose, and neglects to do it in accordance with the word of God. The Lord requires a tithe of a half shekel at the numbering, to support the tabernacle and His priests. Something the sweet psalmist of Israel should know, as David writes in the Psalms, *O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.* And yet...

So with the numbering done the wrong way and the punishment in Exodus being a plague against Israel, the means and reason for punishment are established because David did not resist Satan in this thing.

God sends a prophet named Gad to tell David of His displeasure, and the Lord offers David a choice of punishment, (though we know from Exodus how this will end up going) and David throws himself and all Israel on the mercy of the Lord.

The angel of death comes upon them, and 70,000 men are slain. But as the destroyer came to Jerusalem, the Lord repents and stays the angel's hand, by the threshing floor of Araunah.

This is similar in a way to the Great Tribulation;

**Matthew 24:21-22**
*For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.*

Jesus tells us that for the sake of the believers on earth midway through the Tribulation, before the Rapture and the wrath to follow, God cuts short the works of the beast, least no flesh remain.

And David as a picture of Christ, takes on the sin of Israel and asks the Lord to punish him alone for the sake of his "sheep."

God through the prophet Gad, speaks to David and tells him to set up an altar at the threshinghouse, and David buys the place and the animals for sacrifice which Araunah had offered to give, knowing that David must pay for the sins of the people that the plague may be stayed. Just as Jesus paid it all that we be spared Hell.

teachings.title: David the king as servant
teachings.summary: David's last words confess the Psalms were inspired and show him as a servant king, a picture of Christ and an example of esteeming others better than ourselves.
teachings.text:
The end of David's life is come, and the final words of the King are recorded, and they begin with a beautiful recitation of faith and doctrine.

David, the anointed of God of Jacob, the sweet psalmist of Israel, acknowledges that he was inspired by God, Who spoke through him in the Psalms. In case there was any doubt about the inspiration of the Psalms of David, which were quoted throughout the New Testament by Jesus and the Apostles. *The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and His word was in my tongue*.

David goes further to say the God of Israel, the Rock of Israel, spake to him and advised that he as King must be just, ruling in the fear of God. This is the truth, and a standard that David, being human didn't always achieve.

But it is undeniable as we read his life story that he strove to rule as a God fearing judge, with mercy and faith. An example in patience and longsuffering for Christian believers. He tried to be as the light of the morning, which is how Jesus is described in scripture, that the people of Israel would be as the tender grass covered in dew springs forth at the light. Putting the profit of others before himself, something we are commanded to in scripture;

**Philippians 2:3-5**
*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus*

David is a picture of the king as servant. A picture of Christ, and an example for us who follow after Jesus.

teachings.title: Look and live: the brazen serpent and John 3
teachings.summary: Shows from John 3 that, like Israel looking at the serpent, anyone who believes is saved without turning from sins or doing anything but looking and living, and will be raised on the last day.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
***And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

When Moses lifted up the serpent, all who looked upon it were saved from the venom of the fiery serpents. All who looked and believed were healed. They did not have to turn from their sin. They did not have to make the serpent the Lord of their lives. They did not have to do anything but look and live. 

Jesus Christ tells us that this is a figure of the salvation that He came to bring the world, that through Him man is saved. That God the Father so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son. And all who BELIEVE, that is trust that Jesus died for them and nothing else, are justified. Given eternal life. 

As Jesus says again in **John 6:37-40**

*All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that **every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.***

Not might. Not if they deserve it. Not if they have repented enough to please some man or group of men, but that see Jesus and believe, and they have eternal life and shall in no ways be cast out. Because the Father's will is that all who look to Christ, raised upon the cross and believe that was for our sin, have eternal life. Will be raised on the last day. 

If you are trusting in anything else but Christ on the cross, and the hope of the promise of resurrection of which He was the first fruit, repent. Think again. And if you don't believe that gift is eternal, that Jesus WILL raise you up on that last day, that your works are needed to keep you in grace, repent. Think again. All who believe are not condemned. All who believe HAVE eternal life in Christ. All who believe WILL be raised on the last day. Amen

teachings.title: Jonathan and David's covenant in the Lord
teachings.summary: The covenant of Jonathan and David sworn in the Lord's name pictures salvation, and Jonathan's love above his own father and kingdom shows how we should love Christ and our brethren.
teachings.text:
It is impossible to read this chapter, and miss the number of times both Jonathan and David appeal to the Lord in their communication with each other.

*God forbid; thou shalt not die*...

*David sware moreover...truly as the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step between me and death.*

*And Jonathan said unto David, O Lord God of Israel, when I have sounded my father about to morrow any time, or the third day, and, behold, if there be good toward David, and I then send not unto thee, and shew it thee; The Lord do so and much more to Jonathan: but if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will shew it thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace: and the Lord be with thee, as he hath been with my father. And thou shalt not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of the Lord, that I die not...But also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever: no, not when the Lord hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.*

*So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let the Lord even require it at the hand of David's enemies...*

*If I expressly say unto the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee, take them; then come thou: for there is peace to thee, and no hurt; as the Lord liveth. But if I say thus unto the young man, Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way: for the Lord hath sent thee away. And as touching the matter which thou and I have spoken of, behold, the Lord be between thee and me for ever...*

*And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever.*

The parallel with salvation, calling upon the living God, the Lord God of Israel, literally of the seed of David, and these paths sworn between Jonathan and David are obvious. Saul, like the remnant of unbelieving Jews, having the kingdom taken from him, and given to another, and so he seeks the son of Jesse's life. Just as they sought Christ's.

But Jonathan loves David more than his own father, more than his own earthly reward, more than even inheriting a kingdom of man. No greater love. We should love our brothers in Christ this much. We should love Jesus like this and more.

teachings.title: Eli's house cut off, a faithful priest raised
teachings.summary: The cutting off of Eli's house pictures the end of the Levitical priesthood and the old testament, replaced by Christ the High Priest and the New Testament believers as His royal priesthood.
teachings.text:
The second half of the chapter establishes the narrative of Samuel, and how, as Corban, a gift set aside for the Lord, Elkanah and Hannah gave their young son to Eli the High Priest, to be in service to the Lord.

We learn that as Samuel grew, learning the station of the Levitical priesthood he was part of, even with a linen ephod, he grew in favor with both the Lord and man.

But Eli had two sons serving at the Tabernacle, Hophni and Phinehas, who were reprobates. Sons of Belial. And they profaned the offerings brought before them, taking the choicest cuts, and demanding more of those seeking to keep the offerings of the Law. To the point where they offended many from even bothering with the sacrifices.

These reprobates even were fornicating with the women who gathered at the door of the Tabernacle, abusing their station for their own wicked lusts. And Eli knew, but did not cast them out to be stoned. He allowed them to continue in their evil ways.

And so, the Lord sent a prophet, a man of God, who preached to Eli about the evil the Lord was going to visit upon him and his house. That though God had made a promise to Aaron and his seed to be high priests, that promise was now void;

*Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people? Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.*

The prophet continues speaking the word of God, saying;

*And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.*

This is a picture of what many professing Christians derisively call "replacement theology."

While the immediate meaning of the prophecy is found in the Lord promise to slay Hophni and Phinehas in one day, cutting off the house of Eli and giving Samuel the honor as a faithful priest, it is also a picture of the cutting off of the Levitical priesthood and the OT ceremonial laws and ordinances, and establishing Jesus as His anointed, a High Priest forever, and the NT believers as His royal priesthood.

Replacing physical Israel with the spiritual Israel. Making the Old Testament with the people null by their inability to keep their side of the deal, and so done away with by the death of Christ, and a new testament given by the shedding of His blood;

**Hebrews 9:16-22**
*For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.*

teachings.title: Rahab and the scarlet thread
teachings.summary: Rahab the harlot was saved by her faith in God and placed in the line of Christ, her scarlet thread a picture of His blood, showing God can redeem anyone who holds the faith.
teachings.text:
And so we are here in **Joshua** chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land.

His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in **Numbers 13**, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good.

Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear.

Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan.

She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved.

Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible.

And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew;

**Matthew 1:5-6**
*And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias*

The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread.

And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in **Hebrews 11**, in the company of great Old Testament believers;

**Hebrews 11:31**
*By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace*.

She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart;

**James 2:25**
*Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?*

Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith.

teachings.title: The law was perfect, the fault the people's
teachings.summary: With Joshua as a picture of Christ, he teaches the song of Moses shows the covenant failed because of the people, not the law, which disproves dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
The life of Moses, to whom the law was given, nears its end, and Joshua, a picture of Christ, is given power to lead the children of Israel into the promised land.

Like John, a voice crying out in the wilderness, Moses cleared the way, making the paths straight for the one who would come to bring deliverance.

The book of the law is written, and placed in the Ark that is in the heart of the camp. Done to bear witness of the sins and iniquity of the people. Like the law written in the hearts of man, a conscience, pricked of the Spirit to lay bare our transgressions. To let us know when we have gone astray. As a testimony of the Lord against them who were given the oracles of God. To remind them of their need for His salvation.

An ordinance is given, that in the jubilee year, at the fall feast of Tabernacles, the feast of tents, the people shall gather and hear the reading of the Law. The story of God and His people. His Commandments and His love for them that believe on His name. How he rescued them from bondage and delivered on the promises He made. Every 7 years the people will be reminded. And yet He knows their hearts.

And so the Lord teaches Moses a new song. One to teach the children of Israel that they may know that God knows, they will break the covenant.

This song and its need are all the evidence we need to understand that the fault of the covenant made in the wilderness was always the people. The law itself pure and perfect. The people forsake the God who delivered them, and chase after other gods. God promises to forsake them in turn, for all the evils that they wrought.

Moses, delivering this all to the people before the congregation, reiterates his own knowledge that they will turn aside. That they will utterly corrupt themselves.

Once again, proving dispensationalism to be unbiblical heresy.

teachings.title: Regulating polygamy is not condoning it
teachings.summary: He teaches the firstborn law for a man with two wives regulates sin but does not approve polygamy, and tentatively sees Christ as the firstborn heir.
teachings.text:
*If a man have two wives, one beloved, and another hated, and they have born him children, both the beloved and the hated*...

This instruction is given because God wants to make it clear that in those unique cases where He has chosen the younger to receive the inheritance and blessing, it isn't the standard but the exception. What these verses do not teach is that man should have more than one wife. Only that if they do, and a situation arrives like Abraham's or Isaac's, the proper order of things is to treat the firstborn in the manner of the law, having the double portion, the inheritance and the blessings that come with it.

As with putting away a wife for fornication isn't what is right, but given because of the hardness of our hearts, noting that people might engage in polygamy, giving doctrine to not compound the sin is not condoning the sin.

There is also a picture of Christ, the children of Israel and the salvation offered to the Jews, a new nation bringing forth the fruit thereof. God put away Israel after the flesh for their whoredoms, but Christ is the first born Son of the Lord, and to Him fall all the blessings and inheritance of God. Even though God despised Israel, salvation came of Judah. I am not dogmatic on this interpretation but it seems to hold some lesson along those lines, at least to me.

teachings.title: The Sabbath a picture of rest in Christ
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Sabbath pictures our rest in Jesus, that we contribute no works to salvation, and that those who add works damn themselves.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.*

Profaning His holy name, using it as a curse or to make a false vow, all take His name in vain. But worse are those who claim to be from God, using the name of the Lord to bring a false gospel or to justify evil.

*Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee. Six days thou shalt labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou*.

The Sabbath has always been a picture of Christ, and the rest we have in Jesus. And the prohibition against working on that day was to illustrate that we contribute nothing to our salvation except to honor His sacrifice by trusting on Him to justify us before God.

It is a gift of God, not of works, least any man should boast.

Again, there are no equivocations or rationalizations that can possibly justify those who add their works to God's plan of salvation, given us in Christ. They damn themselves just as assuredly as the man who gathered wood in the wilderness on the Sabbath. Salvation by grace through faith without works has been the Gospel from the beginning.

teachings.title: The drink offering is no warrant for strong drink
teachings.summary: The strong wine poured out with the continual burnt offering was a libation to God, a figure of Christ's blood, and gives no cover for drinking or for fermented wine at the Lord's supper, since priests were forbidden strong drink.
teachings.text:
As the book of **Numbers** begins to wind down, and Moses nears the end of his life, the Lord reiterates His ordinances and feasts. There is a new high priest. The men of the first generation having all died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua.

The Lord lays out the requirements for the continual burnt sacrifices and sabbath sacrifices and the offerings made for sin.

Each has its specific requirements, varying by the day or type. The offerings of lambs or kids or bullocks. The flour and oil to be given. And the drink offerings poured out.

All a picture of Jesus. All a continuous savor to the Lord. As the children of Israel reach the promised land, they are called to remember these ordinances for all time, that their faith in the Lord not be forgotten, and His favor given them.

Verse 7 contains a description of the drink offering.

*And the drink offering thereof shall be the fourth part of an hin for the one lamb: in the holy place shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured unto the Lord for a drink offering.*

This is a verse that could be used to defend the consumption of alcohol, or the blasphemy of using fermented wine at the Lord's supper, although it rarely is.

But the prohibition against the priests consumption of strong wine;

**Leviticus 10:8-9**
*And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying, Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations:*

...and the numerous places in scripture that teach against it present a problem for those seeking to use this verse to justify it.

But what then? First, we see the drink offering is to be poured out with the burnt offering, which is a continual fire. Alcoholic strong drink would feed the fire, where new wine would quench it. Also, where fermented juices store easily, there is the idea that in the wilderness it would be easiest to obtain and have on hand for the purpose of a twice daily sacrifice.

Ellicott's Commentary states:
(7) Shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured . . . --Better, pour out the drink offering of strong drink. The word shecar, which is here rendered "strong wine," denotes any kind of intoxicating drink, whether made from grapes, honey, or grain; but it is more frequently used to denote a drink which is not made from grapes, as, e.g., in Leviticus 10:9, where the command is given to Aaron and his sons not to drink "wine nor strong drink" (shecar) when they went into the tent of meeting. In the parallel passage in Exodus, the drink offering was to consist of "the fourth part of an hin of wine" (Numbers 29:40). (Comp. Numbers 15:5.) In Exodus 30:9 it is forbidden to pour any drink offering upon the altar of incense, from which passage it has been inferred that the drink offerings were poured upon the altar of burnt sacrifice.

The indication that strong wine is liquor from other sources than grapes, which has weak fermentation.

Matthew Henry commentary says;
The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17.

I only note these to show that this passage is unique in what it commands, and the reason unclear other than to suppose it is a libation for God, and His will it be offered.

teachings.title: The gospel is not 200 years old
teachings.summary: Traces the same salvation by faith in the sacrifice of the Lamb from Adam and Eve, Abel and Cain, and Enos in Genesis 4:26 to answer the claim that the gospel is new.
teachings.text:
There is a resurgence of unsaved people using the false argument that the Gospel by which we are saved is "only 200 years old." Many heresies come in cycles. You will see the same one suddenly pop-up from multiple people, and it is currently the trending heresy I am witnessing. 

The idea that the same salvation of Genesis is "new," is absurd. 

Adam and Eve, having sinned, sought to cover themselves with figleaves they sowed themselves. God corrected them and showed them, covering their sins with the lamb skins He provided, the blood shed representing Christ's, the redemption by faith. 

Righteous Abel believed God and He pleased the Lord. Cain sought to offer his own works and God rebuked him. And Cain in his pride became the first reprobate. 

**Genesis 4:26**
*And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

This is the same Gospel as we preach today. Faith in the sacrifice God offered for us. Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Justified in the blood. Covered by the snow white wool of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. 

Amen.

teachings.title: Jerusalem's fall a picture of the great tribulation
teachings.summary: Zedekiah's fall pictures the end: the pillars and holy vessels taken are the saints broken in the great tribulation, a remnant brought out, and the King lifted up as Christ.
teachings.text:
Zedekiah did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done. Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

The Lord sends Babylon against Judah to punish them for their transgressions, and Zedekiah and the people harden their hearts and rebel against Nebuchadnezzar rather than repent towards God. And the Lord's wrath comes upon them, and they are besieged. For a year and a half Jerusalem are starved out by the Chaldean horde surrounding them.

They die of famine and pestilence and war. Just as the unbelieving are slaughtered by the horsemen.

The city is torn down, not one stone remaining upon another. They are made desolate. Empty.

The king and his men flee to the wilderness and are captured. Zedekiah brought before the king for judgment. His seed is sniffed out before his eyes, and then he is blinded. Blind unto his death.

Just as the Jews who rebelled against God were blinded, those who believed not on the Lord Jesus Christ. Blind and imprisoned until their death. Cut off.

Then Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard carried away certain of the poor, the residue of the people. A remnant.

The rest fell away, fell to the king of Babylon. The multitude. A falling away.

But there was a remnant saved, and left behind to be vinedressers and husbandmen, tasked with bringing in the harvest. The increase of which belongs to the lord set over them. Just as Christians are, to bring forth fruit. After their kind. Servants of the Lord.

The pillars of the temple were taken away. Broken down. Carried off to Babylon. Just as believers are the pillars of the temple of God, the body of Christ that is the church of believers. Just as we who are alive and remain will be broken by the antichrist when he makes war on the saints. Just as the abomination that maketh desolate will break the pillars, the saints.

And the cauldrons and bowls and spoons and sniffers and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered. The holy vessels, used to minister, the same are saved Christians. Vessels of the Lord fitted for His purpose. Taken away. The refined silver. The brass. The pillars. This is the great tribulation and the martyrdom of the saints.

And the 7 kings who set up Zedekiah, and his scribe, and the guards and all the ministers of the false king. A picture of the Beast and his prophet and the seven horns that give him his power...they are smote by the King set over them by God.

But there are carried away a remnant who live. Who are brought out of great tribulation to serve the king. And the king of Babylon (at this time Evilmeridach), suffered not to leave Jehoiachin in prison, and lifted up Jehoiachin, to sit at his right hand. To be king of kings. Where he would eat bread every day of his life. Just as God the Father has lifted up His Son, the Lord Jesus.

teachings.title: The jubilee pictures Christ's redemption
teachings.summary: The sabbatical years and jubilee picture Christ as near kinsman redeemer, with the trumpet of jubilee pointing to His second coming and our redemption.
teachings.text:
Leviticus chapter 25 brings us the law of Jubilee, a perpetual sabbatical observation of the 7th year, in the land of Canaan which the Lord brought the children of Israel, culminating in the 49th year, 7 times 7, a jubilee, a proclamation of liberty, wherein all God's children shall be redeemed.

Of course this parallels with Christ, and the redemption from the bonds of sin He makes for us, as the near kin, the Son of man, setting us free.

The particulars of this law, which wouldn't take effect for the Isralites until they had settled the land, driving out the former inhabitants and dividing by lot the tribes and the habitations thereof, showed not only the foresight of God's providence, but His terms as the actual owner, the land Lord so to speak, of the land He gives them.

And so, 6 years the fields are sown and the vineyards dressed, but in the 7th, there was no work to be done in the land. God promises them that the 6th year will be bountiful enough to tide them over to the 9th year, that they could live off their stores, because God provides all. Not of their own works.

The timing of the jubilee, which was marked in the 49th year, 7 sabbaths, was marked at the end of the fall feasts by the trumpets at the end of the day of atonement.

Just as Pentecost is celebrating the 7th sabbath after Passover, the spring feasts, represent Christs work here at His first coming, then the Jubilee is marked by the fall feast, which is emblematic of His second, and the day of redemption for believers. The trumpet sounds to announce the victory of the Lord, the atonement bought with blood, the redemption from bondage and the liberty given all, rich or poor.

teachings.title: The shewbread and the Lord of the sabbath
teachings.summary: The lamps and shewbread picture God's truth and word, and religion that forgets their meaning becomes rote practice used to condemn, as with the Pharisees.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 24** begins with the command to have the lamps of the Tabernacle burn continually, dusk to dawn. A statute for ever. That there is light in the place of God.

And God commands that there be bread baked as a memorial, continually, as an offering before the Lord, and eaten by the Levitical priests. This is called the shewbread, concentrated by the Lord.

The light symbolizes the truth of God throughout the Bible, and so it is never dark before Him. The bread is both the life given the people by God's grace and His word.

This shewbread becomes a means of feeding David and his men as they flee Saul, who was in a murderous rage against the future king. Even as it was offered to God and holy, but to the Lord's purpose, it fed His favored in a time of need.

Likewise, as Jesus rebukes the Pharisees when He and His disciples gleaned corn on the Sabbath to eat, Jesus points to how these things are the Lord's, and not just blind tradition and meaningless ritual. That He is the Lord of the sabbath.

Often religion becomes rote practices, that forget the meaning behind them as the Pharisees had. Using these things to condemn. Jesus says had they understood who He was, that He was present for mercy in His death and resurrection to come, that the sacrifices of the temple were a picture of Him who had come not to condemn but to save, that they'd understand why it was acceptable for them to eat of their work, as the Levites were allowed on the sabbath. Because they did the work of God.

teachings.title: Israel saved by the blood before the law
teachings.summary: Israel was delivered from Egypt by faith in the passover blood before receiving the law, so those who demand turning from sin before believing reverse God's order.
teachings.text:
Now the salvation of the children of Israel from Egypt, that are freed from the yoke of bondage, came in faith on the promise of God. That by the blood of the Passover offering they are spared death. That by the waters they passed through, baptized into a new people and brought to a land promised them of God. Flowing with milk and honey, a land taken by those who failed to fear and serve the living God, but set about to establish their own righteousness. And then sanctified by the Lord to His purpose.

This historical and physical story is a picture of the spiritual, and the individual salvation of us who believe and are adopted by God as His people.

And so we should notice the order of things; salvation is front loaded and found only by faith. For the salvation of Israel from bondage and death came by faith alone, by the blood.

The Isralites in Egypt were not told to change their ways first. To become holy first. To repent of their sins and throw themselves before God crying for mercy because of how wicked they were.

God decided in His grace to offer them mercy if they believed Moses and Aaron, and trusted in the blood of the lamb.

And so all Israel was saved.

Then they were baptized together. Then they were given God's law. Then they were told to sanctify themselves, for their own good and to better serve God's will.

Those who place the giving of the law before the acceptance of faith are in error. Those telling others they must turn from their sins first before they can believe are entangling them in bondage. Placing the yoke upon those who should be set free.

teachings.title: The Lord, merciful and gracious, and Jealous
teachings.summary: In Exodus 34 God reveals Himself as merciful yet not clearing the guilty and as Jealous, guarding His people, while the feasts all picture Christ.
teachings.text:
*Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.*

Exodus chapter 34 finds Moses in need to hew the rocks into tablets to replace those he broke in his anger at the golden calf and the sin of the children of Israel. The first God hewn, now must be made by Moses that God could give to him the covenant as a record, written in stone.

Only Moses was allowed on Saini, not even the beasts of the field were allowed to graze the foothills nearby.

The Lord came in a cloud and the figure of Christ Jesus (IMO) appeared before him, as the glory of the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed "*The Lord, The Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.*

This is who God is. We who are saved seek to know Him and throughout scripture we are given many names and descriptions that allow us to understand the holy God. Here is the quality of God that is judgment. He is merciful and longsuffering. He forgives. But He does not clear the guilty, and he visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third or fourth generation.

That is not to say they are punished for the sins of the father, but rather their inequities being judgment upon their people for generations. God is about to declare a genocide of the people in the way towards the promised land. The wickedness they have done in His sight. The groves and high places, molten gods and altars. God tells Moses that they are to destroy these people that their wickedness doesn't infect the children of Israel, through practice, through marriage, or in any way including eating meat sacrificed to idols.

We learn a name for God and it is Jealous. He is a jealous God. Jealousy is not envy or covetousness. It is fiercely protecting that which one owns. God is saying in this covenant He owns them, they are His people. And if they go whoring after strange gods because they were snared by covenant to make peace with the people He has judged be destroyed, He will have vengeance upon the children of Israel.

To further defend what is His from whoredoms, going after strange gods, the Lord further emphasizes the ordinances for feasts He has put in place as a memorial for what He has done for the people of Israel, and as a picture of the Messiah to come, Christ Jesus.

The feast of unleavened bread that begins immediately after Passover, which is the sabbaths of Christ when He is 3 days and 3 nights in Hell for our sins. And because His only begotten Son is a sacrifice for us, and because the firstborn sons of the children of Israel were spared in passover, even if their cattle, they belong to God and must be attoned through a substitutionary sacrifice. All a picture of Christ.

The sabbath, again a picture of Christ.

The feast of weeks, which leads to the Pentecost. The firstfruits of the harvest.

Then the feast of the harvest at years end.

All a picture of the time to come, and a memorial for the children of Israel that they may know Jesus.

*Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning.*

The unleavened bread and unfermented wine of the Lord's supper. Taking Jesus down from the cross before sunset on Passover.

The first of the firstfruits are God's under this Mosaic law. All a picture of Christ.

teachings.title: The entire Bible teaches one faith in Christ
teachings.summary: What is mocked as replacement theology is simply the Bible's one theme of salvation in Christ from Moses to Revelation, which dispensationalism denies.
teachings.text:
The entire Bible teaches what is derisively called replacement theology. Better phrased; The entire Bible teaches the one faith of salvation and redemption in Christ. The failure of man in the flesh to find holiness in the works of their own righteousness, and the grace and mercy of God in providing a sacrifice for their sin that they may know Him. For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.

Moses wrote of Jesus, in Genesis. In Exodus. In Leviticus and Deuteronomy. The prophets spoke of Him, and preached His gospel of redemption and reconciliation. The Psalms sing of Him and His coming. Jesus Christ in the flesh spent 3.5 years of an earthly ministry reaching the lost sheep of Israel that He could lead who were His, calling them to repentance and preaching to the unbelieving that they were going to be replaced and cast into outer darkness with wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Once the veil is torn at the death of Christ, the remaining scripture teaches of the gospel given to a people who were not a nation, now heirs to the Kingdom. The branches that did not produce fruit meet for repentance, cast into the fire.

The epistles giving us the grafting in, the theology of salvation and religion undefiled. The Revelation of Christ Jesus, the rapture of believers, the resurrection, adoption and redemption God predestined in His Son. And God's final judgement that we may know it, and come to Him before it's too late.

And it is this simple truth, the entire theme of scripture, that the false doctrine of dispensationalism denies and rejects.

teachings.title: Ordinances were pictures, not idols
teachings.summary: The Old Testament ordinances like the sabbath were shadows of Christ ended at the cross, but the Pharisees, like Israel with the brazen serpent, made the picture an idol and a work of self-righteousness.
teachings.text:
In chapter 5, and now again in Luke chapter 6, we see the Pharisees seeking to accuse Jesus, that they may discredit Him and His growing ministry. Particularly, they are seeking to shame Him and His disciples for their failure to keep certain ordinances, carnal ceremony, given both by tradition and under the law of Moses, among these ordinances are things like the fasting of meats(food), ceremonial washings(**Matthew 15:12**) and the keeping of the sabbath, the day of rest, as we see here.

The Bible says these ordinances were given in the OT as a picture, a shadow, to remind the people of the promise of the coming Christ, that they not forget and hold fast to the faith preached unto them, until the *day of reformation*. That is, until the things they are foreshadowing come true. Until Christ comes. At that time Jesus figuratively nails them to the cross with Himself. They are over and done, having served their purpose.

And, with the ordinances ended, the Bible says, so too was the regard God had for the nation of Israel. They were to either believe or perish, the same as the Gentiles. Thus the destruction of the Temple in 70AD, least any confusion remain.

And of these ordinances, the keeping of the sabbath was probably the most important, that the people would enter into God's rest, understanding that His work was finished at the time of creation. A picture man could understand, working 6 days and resting the 7th as God did. Forbidden work, because God did it all in regards to salvation. It is a picture of salvation by faith alone in His perfect, meaning complete, works, finished by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

But man is simple, and foolish and superstitious. The things of God that are a physical picture of the spiritual application He seeks to teach us, becomes an end unto itself in vain tradition. Many, with an autistically literal approach, put the power in the picture, not the things that are being pictured.

And example is given in the OT, in **Numbers 21** where by unbelief the Hebrews in the desert were beset by poisonous snakes, fiery serpents. Many were bit and were dying in agony. God, as an object lesson in the Christ to come, had Moses lift up a brazen snake, made of molten brass and formed, upon a tall wooden pole. This represented Christ and the crucifixion, where Jesus became all sin for us. He said to the people if you look up on this picture of salvation you'll be healed. Lesson learned.

We know this was a picture of Jesus, because it was explained in **John 3**:

*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.*

But we are told that hundreds of years later, the Israelites had lost the purpose and understanding that this picture served. In **2 Kings 4** Hezekiah became king and had to right many of the wrongs in the land;

*He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.*

The picture of the spiritual became a physical idol. The Heavenly lesson became bonds of the carnal.

This is where the Pharisees, Sadducees and scribes are at in the time of Christ. They have lost sight of the spiritual application for these things, and worship the symbol instead.

And so the carnal ordinances were to them an idol. And the work of their flesh in keeping these things replaced their faith in the Lord. They became self-righteous. They used the keeping of these ordinances as how one becomes righteous, rather than faith in what it represents, the Christ to come. And so, they become holier than thou  hypocrites. And later, Judaizers seeking to impose their vain traditions on the newly born again Gentiles. Circumcision, sacrifices, and the keeping of holy days such as the sabbath.

teachings.title: Christ Offered Once to Bear Our Sins
teachings.summary: Substitutionary atonement teaches that Christ's blood, pictured by the old sacrifices, sealed the better testament and removed the veil between God and man.
teachings.text:
Substitutionary atonement, also called vicarious atonement, the Biblical understanding Jesus Christ being the sacrifice that takes away the sins of the whole world, to the salvation of those who believe, is laid out here (and throughout scripture) as the blood needed to affirm the promise made by God the Father. Just as the blood of bulls and goats was used to seal the covenant with Moses, or marked by Abraham with his promise from God.

But these sacrifices were for a time and a place and acted as a picture for the perfect sacrifice of Jesus Christ, Whose blood marked the promise of a better testament, one in which the separation from God pictured by the temple, the veils, the Levitical priests, dietary laws, marking of days and carnal ordinances of the Old Testament is done away with.

Here at the end of the world, Jesus was offered once and put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself. And in doing so, became our High Priest, and we who believe adopted sons, a holy priesthood. The separation from God is gone. The veil torn asunder.

Many false religions posing as Christians deny the idea that Jesus was the sacrifice that gave us the offer of God's mercy. They deny the grace of a loving God who bought them with the price of His Son. That the shedding of blood and the remission of sins isn't the way, but instead these thorns and briars produce evil fruit that cannot repent from dead works to serve the living God.

But the Bible teaches us the truth of the matter. That Jesus as the sole mediator between God and man was by the means of His death, becoming sin for the redemption of transgressions. (For sin is the transgression of the law).

A testament having no power while the testator liveth. And so the death of the testator signified that those called had come into their promised inheritance. Amen.

So Christ was offered once to bear our sins. And those of us who believed look to His coming to our day of redemption. The Spirit as the surety of the promise, a testimony within us to the truth of God's word.

teachings.title: The Whore and the Bride
teachings.summary: The whore and the Lamb's bride are set in contrast: trusting idols, rites or works is spiritual adultery against a jealous God.
teachings.text:
There is an interesting contrast made in the opening verse of chapter 17, and a verse from chapter 21:

**Revelation 17:1**
*And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:*

Revelation 21:9
*And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.*

The whore represents the unsaved and the wicked. The saved as the Lamb's wife, a bride.

The contrast and context of faithfulness and purity is intentional. A parable for a God whose name is Jealous.

*For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.*

As Jesus teaches in Matthew 5:28

*But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.*

The same is true for us spiritually. When we put other gods before Him, even in our hearts, or trust in something other than Him to be our Lord and savior, it is adultery.

To make your faith one of idols and rites and vain traditions, trusting in our works and institutions made of man over the Lord who bought you, it is whoremongering. It is fornication.

And all those who lead others to this, especially when they claim the name of Christ Jesus, are harlots. Whores. And they serve the beast.

teachings.title: The World Hates an Evil Report of Sin
teachings.summary: As Joseph's brothers hated him for his evil report, the world hates faithful Christians because preaching against sin exposes their deeds.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 37** begins the tale of Joseph and Judah, the other brothers and how the sons of Jacob came to be in Egypt. The generations of Israel, told by God through Moses. In this narrative, there lays prophecy of Christ Jesus, both as a figure in Joseph and in the blessing upon Judah, which we will see later near the end.

But keeping in mind the picture of Jesus in Joseph and the traits of man in the brothers, especially Judah/Jews of Christ's time, there's a lot to digest.

First, we are given the timing and situation; Joseph, the first son born unto Rachel, Jacob's first love, and so the father's favorite. Joseph, out with his half brothers tending the flocks returns to his father, bringing an "evil report." Bringing word to the father that the children are in sin.

And the brothers hate him for it.

Much the same way today the world hates a faithful Christian for the reminder of their sin we bring. The light shined on their inequity. As Jesus says in **John 3:20**:

*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.*

Christians standing fast against sin bring an evil report of the wicked hearts of men. The world resents it.

**John 15:18** I*f the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.*

Joseph's brothers hated him for the same reason. Sinners hate preaching against sin. Standards and morality. God's word, which convicts them. Christians who bring an evil report to their deeds.

And like Joseph's brothers, the world plots and schemes ways to shut us up. To sully Christ's name by our own failings. To discredit God's word. To subvert His people. To call good evil and evil good.

[Isaiah 5:20](https://t.me/ApeMtn37/3516)
*Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!*

teachings.title: He believed, and it was counted for righteousness
teachings.summary: Abram's faith in the promised seed was imputed to him for righteousness, and the sacrifices of Genesis 15 pictured Christ's blood offering.
teachings.text:
That's a lot of Bible this morning, and I didn't even get as deep as we could on this, but it's all fundamental to understanding the Gospel, and who is the seed of Abraham, how he blessed all nations. How through that seed, Abraham had multitudes too numerous to count as heirs to the promise made when he called upon the name of the Lord. The promise made when *he believed in the Lord; and He counted it to him for righteousness.* That his righteousness was imputed for that faith, by a gracious God. And it was faith in that seed to be given by the Lord, and the blessings for that heir and the promise made in Him.

As we will see in Esau and Jacob, the blessings and promises of the heir are important. The free will choices made by man, and faith in God determining who received them, not the law. For under the law the eldest received the inheritance. And the blessing.

*And he said,* Lord God, *whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?* And the word of God tells him to sacrifice *an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.*

Each a sign or a picture of Christ. As established in the Levitical laws, 400+ years from when this is happening, done to show they mercy of God in redemption by faith, in the blood offerings, the sin offerings, the burnt offerings. A testimony necessitates a blood offering. These were a symbol of Christ's.

And in a deep sleep, a darkness fell upon Abram, and the word of God said; *Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* prophesying the time to come and the sojourning to Egypt and enslavement. *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* Moses writing in the Spirit of the prophecy of Exodus given to Abraham.

*And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age. But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.*

The LORD telling Abram that he himself will die knowing peace, but that the land will not be given unto his descendants until the wickedness of the Amorites comes in. They are going to purge the land of Canaan of the wicked, as an instrument of the Lord. Against *The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites, And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,*
*And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.*

And a furnace and a lamp appeared on the offerings, passing between those pieces laid on an altar, a testament signed by God.

teachings.title: Christ the bridegroom and the whore of Babylon
teachings.summary: Scripture pictures God's people as a bride and idolatry as adultery and whoredom, which is why the Roman Catholic Church is shown as the whore of Babylon, mother of harlots.
teachings.text:
Throughout scripture, God's relationship to His people is likened unto a marriage, Christ Jesus as the bridegroom, believers the bride. And just as married couples are joined together, become of one flesh, and adultery an abomination, so too scripture refers to chasing after false gods and idols as adultery.

The fornication with which a man may put away his betrothed is a like symbol of God's putting away a people who have gone after strange gods. He also calls it whoredom.

Scripture says to suffer not a harlot of the daughters of Israel, and it is both literal and symbolic of the call by God to be faithful unto Him.

That is why the Roman Catholic Church, the Whore of Babylon, mother of harlots, is represented this way. The cup of her fornication. It's all relative in terms to the bride, the believers in Christ who remain faithful.

The institution of marriage itself is a parable by which God teaches us of fidelity, and what it means to be a jealous God. How the man is head of the house, one body and one flesh with his wife, just as Jesus is head of His body, made up of the saints.

The one world religion of works and many gods will be used by the beast to gain control, until they turn on the whore and install the antichrist in the temple, proclaiming himself as God, Christ returned.

teachings.title: No limbo: Old Testament saints were saved by faith
teachings.summary: Shows that Adam and all Old Testament saints went to Heaven by faith in God's word, and that Limbo and purgatory are inventions. Points to Christ as the lamb slain before the foundation of the world and the blood on the mercy seat.
teachings.text:
No they didn't. "Limbo" is an invention of the RCC. 

Saved Christians know that Adam, and all OT saints, went to Heaven, the same way we do; faith in God's word. Jesus went to Hell to pay the price for all sin, Adam's to yours, and beyond. He freed the saved in the Old Testament the same way He's freed us. With His blood. 

Repent and get saved today! It's a free gift from God, and no institutions of man can give it to you, or deny His grace to you.

The Bible says that Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. That He was "foreordained before the foundation of the world." All believers were called upon to "inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The notion of Limbo comes from unsaved false prophets, like Clement of Alexandria, who not understanding simple salvation, sought to rectify the ways of God to the feeble understanding of a natural man, stating that "it's not right" that the Patriarchs, "should be condemned without trial," when the wages of sin has always been death. Natural man questioning God's judgement is the source of most heresy. 

The scriptures teach us that there are none righteous, "no not one," and that since the first generation of man, we have been justified by faith alone calling upon the name of the Lord. 

Heaven and Hell. Those are the two choices before every man. There is no limbo. There is no purgatory. There is no working your way to righteousness. There is only the blood of the lamb on the mercy seat. The burnt offering of Christ. Amen.
